sentences.zh: 他们是在半夜发现的，当时有人向警察报告说，嘿，公园里好像有人在施工。

sentences.en: Even the NYPD is not notified.
sentences.zh: 出事了。

sentences.en: They find out in the middle of the night when someone reports to a police officer, hey, it looks like people are building things in the park.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不派警察在早上拦住妈妈们，而此时树木正在被砍倒并切成碎片。

sentences.en: Something's going on.
sentences.zh: 过去，媒体总是称赞摩西的办事方式。

sentences.en: And they have to send police officers in to hold the moms back in the morning while trees are knocked down and being chopped into pieces.
sentences.zh: 他们对那种狡猾的手段睁一只眼闭一只眼。

sentences.en: And the media in the past has always applauded Moses's ways of getting things done.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们称之为“哎呀，抱歉”式的办事方法。

sentences.en: They kind of winked at him for those kind of devious ways.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们倒戈了。

sentences.en: You know, they talked about it was the like, oops, sorry method of getting things done.
sentences.zh: 他们拍到了妈妈们在树木被砍伐时哭泣的照片。

sentences.en: But now they turn on him.
sentences.zh: 这些照片到处都是，可惜书里没有收录。

sentences.en: They got pictures of mothers crying as trees are cut down.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，照片部分是我觉得这本书最令人失望的地方。

sentences.en: They appear everywhere, though unfortunately they're not in this book.
sentences.zh: 但书里确实展示了一张卡罗描述的照片，一个小男孩拿着玩具步枪，而一名警察在围栏旁站岗。

sentences.en: Again, the photo section is the one part of this book that I feel like is such a letdown.
sentences.zh: 照片源源不断地涌现，尴尬的警察、痛苦的母亲、反对摩西的读者来信纷至沓来。

sentences.en: But they do show a photo in the book of a picture Carol describes of a little boy holding a toy rifle as a police officer stands guard at the fence.
sentences.zh: 摩西并没有被摧毁，但这是他第一次真正名誉扫地。

sentences.en: And it's just there's all these photos come in, embarrassed police officers, anguished mothers, anti-Moses letters the editor pour in.
sentences.zh: 卡罗写道：1956年4月24日星期二，罗伯特·摩西派军队进入中央公园的那一天，是罗伯特·摩西的“黑色星期二”。

sentences.en: And Moses is not destroyed, but for the first time he's really tarnished.
sentences.zh: 因为在那一天，他失去了最珍贵的资产——他的名誉。

sentences.en: And Carol writes, Tuesday, April 24th, 1956, the day that Robert Moses sent his troops into Central Park was Robert Moses's Black Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 摩西的繁荣期持续了30年。

sentences.en: For on it he lost his most cherished asset, his reputation.
sentences.zh: 现在，一切都结束了。

sentences.en: The Moses boom had lasted for 30 years.
sentences.zh: 并不是说——在任何人这么想之前，并不是说摩西就此罢手了。

sentences.en: Now it was over.
sentences.zh: 他依然，树木还是被砍倒了。

sentences.en: And it's not like, I mean, before anyone thinks, it's not like then Moses is like, all right, never mind.
sentences.zh: 他确实把那些树砍倒了。

sentences.en: Like he's still, the trees come down.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like he tears those trees down.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，他还在修建当时一些主要的高速公路和桥梁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: And he's like, during this period, he's also building some of the major highways and bridges of this time.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说他的权力完全被削弱了，但就在这件事上，他确实遭受了重创。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This is like, this is not like a complete diminishment of his power, but right here he really takes it on the chin.
sentences.zh: 市长支持他，因为他拥有权力。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 市长需要那种权力。

sentences.en: And the mayor stands behind him because he has the power.
sentences.zh: 但在他开始为这个停车场铺设混凝土之前，发生了一件不同的事情。

sentences.en: The mayor needs that power.
sentences.zh: 还记得1934年吗，他拆除了中央公园赌场（Central Park Casino），人们说你不该这么做。

sentences.en: But something, one thing kind of different happens before he can start laying down the concrete for this parking lot.
sentences.zh: 而州法院说，他想做什么就做什么。

sentences.en: And so remember back in 1934, he tore down the Central Park Casino and people were like, you shouldn't do that.
sentences.zh: 他对公园拥有绝对的权力。

sentences.en: And the state court said, he can do whatever he wants.
sentences.zh: （注：此处原文编号缺失，已根据逻辑补全）

sentences.en: He has total power over the parks.
sentences.zh: （注：此处原文编号缺失，已根据逻辑补全）

sentences.en: Now, 22 years later, it's 1956, and the state Supreme Court, one of the justices, actually grants an injunction halting work pending a hearing.
sentences.zh: 22年后的1956年，州最高法院的一位法官竟然颁布了一项禁令，在听证会结束前叫停了施工。

sentences.en: And this is the kind of thing they didn't even do before, grant these injunctions.
sentences.zh: 而这种颁布禁令的事，他们以前甚至根本不会做。

sentences.en: And Moses is like, I'm going to win this.
sentences.zh: 摩西心想：我一定会赢。

sentences.en: I can get it done my way.
sentences.zh: 我可以用我的方式搞定。

sentences.en: He refuses to compromise.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝妥协。

sentences.en: And that's when Stanley Isaacs, that wily old reformer, he remembers one thing and discovers two things.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，那个精明的老改革派斯坦利·艾萨克斯想起了一件事，又发现了两件事。
zh_words: 改革派斯坦利·艾萨克斯

sentences.en: He remembers that, one, when Moses tore down the original casino to build the tavern,
sentences.zh: 他想起，第一，当初摩西拆除原来的赌场去建这家酒馆时，

sentences.en: he said he made a big stink about how only restaurants with reasonable prices should be in a public park.
sentences.zh: 他曾大张旗鼓地宣称，公园里只应该有价格合理的餐厅。

sentences.en: And by 1956, the tavern's prices are not reasonable.
sentences.zh: 而到了1956年，这家酒馆的价格一点也不合理。

sentences.en: They're charging $4.50 for a hamburger and a beer.
sentences.zh: 他们卖一个汉堡加一杯啤酒要收4.5美元。

sentences.en: And, I mean, that sounds like an amazing deal.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这听起来像是个超值的优惠。

sentences.en: But in 1956, it was not.
sentences.zh: 但在1956年，这可不是。

sentences.en: And Caro quotes one news story.
sentences.zh: 卡罗引用了一篇新闻报道。

sentences.en: He goes, dinner and tip for two came to $23.
sentences.zh: 他说，两个人的晚餐加小费一共花了23美元。

sentences.en: There was another $5 at the bar for two drinks each.
sentences.zh: 吧台还要另付5美元，每人两杯酒。

sentences.en: It's not a place to go the day before payday.
sentences.zh: 这可不是发薪日前会去的地方。

sentences.en: And, again, I'm like, like with the rents we were talking about in previous episodes, I'm salivating over those prices.
sentences.zh: 而且，我还是那句话，就像我们之前几集聊到的租金一样，我对这些价格垂涎三尺。

sentences.en: And it's just it is not – this is not a restaurant the average person could just walk into and buy a hamburger in.
sentences.zh: 但这真的不是普通人能随便走进去买个汉堡吃的餐厅。

sentences.en: And the second and more important thing Isaac discovers is the sweetheart deal that Moses gave to the restaurant's owner, Arnold Schleifer.
sentences.zh: 艾萨克斯发现的第二件、也是更重要的事情，是摩西给餐厅老板阿诺德·施莱弗提供的“甜心交易”。

sentences.en: Schleifer is supposed to pay the city 5% of his gross income, which is already ridiculously low rent for a fancy restaurant in a major city park in a fantastic location.
sentences.zh: 施莱弗本应向市政府支付总收入的5%作为租金，对于一家位于大城市公园绝佳地段的高档餐厅来说，这已经低得离谱了。

sentences.en: But even that percentage, he hasn't been paying because his contract allows him to deduct the cost of improvements to the restaurant from his taxes.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，他连这笔比例的租金都没交，因为合同允许他从税款中扣除餐厅的改建费用。

sentences.en: So Isaac finds that over a four-year period, Schleifer made almost $1.8 million, and he paid the city $9,000 in taxes.
sentences.zh: 所以艾萨克斯发现，在四年时间里，施莱弗赚了近180万美元，却只向市政府缴纳了9000美元的税款。

sentences.en: And Moses is essentially making this guy rich at the city's expense.
sentences.zh: 摩西本质上是在用城市的钱让这家伙发财。

sentences.en: And Caro makes it clear.
sentences.zh: 卡罗把这一点说得很清楚。

sentences.en: The deal is not illegal.
sentences.zh: 这笔交易并不违法。

sentences.en: Moses is not getting a kickback, although the quid pro quo is that Schleifer has to cater every banquet Moses likes.
sentences.zh: 摩西没有拿回扣，尽管交换条件是施莱弗必须承办摩西喜欢的所有宴会。

sentences.en: And we talked in that earlier episode about how Schleifer catered that one banquet in a way that was just a little too fancy-schmancy ethnic for Moses.
sentences.zh: 我们在之前那集聊过，施莱弗承办的那场宴会，对摩西来说显得有点过于花哨、太讲究民族风情了。

sentences.en: And he wrote that great memoir about it.
sentences.zh: 他还为此写了一篇很棒的回忆录。

sentences.en: But this flies in the face of another part of Moses' reputation, this idea that the guy doesn't cater to favoritism, that he doesn't do sweetheart deals.
sentences.zh: 但这与摩西的另一种名声背道而驰，即他从不偏袒、从不做“甜心交易”的形象。

sentences.en: He clearly is.
sentences.zh: 但他显然做了。

sentences.en: And the press can make a lot of hay about this too.
sentences.zh: 媒体也能借此大做文章。

sentences.en: They can oversimplify the story to make it sound more corrupt than it is.
sentences.zh: 他们可以把故事过度简化，让它听起来比实际情况更腐败。

sentences.en: But whereas in the past, the press's oversimplification has helped Moses, now is starting to hurt him.
sentences.zh: 但过去媒体的过度简化曾帮过摩西，现在却开始伤害他了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, he's just like – it's like an infection.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他就像……这就像是一种感染。

sentences.en: Like the mothers and the images of the cute kid with the air rifle and stuff like that, they sort of make a little cut.
sentences.zh: 就像那些母亲们，还有那个拿着气步枪的可爱孩子的照片之类的东西，它们造成了一点小伤口。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden this type of thing, which normally wouldn't cause him any problems whatsoever, are just – there's just enough damage there to infect, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，这种通常根本不会给他带来任何麻烦的事情，就……造成的破坏足以引发感染，你知道的，

sentences.en: and sort of get him off of, you know, his normal game when it comes to this stuff.
sentences.zh: 让他偏离了处理这类事情时的正常节奏。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's just – it's this, you know, chipping away, this little bit of chipping away at the reputation that holds him up.
sentences.zh: 这只是……这是一种蚕食，一点一点地蚕食支撑他的名声。

sentences.en: And I just want to note, it's at this part of the story that we were on page 999 in the book.
sentences.zh: 我只想提一下，故事讲到这里，我们书已经读到第999页了。

sentences.en: We're about to do it, people.
sentences.zh: 我们要做到这一点了，各位。

sentences.en: We're about to tip over into quadruple digits in page numbers.
sentences.zh: 我们马上就要跨入四位数的页码了。

sentences.en: Not something you see in a lot of books.
sentences.zh: 这在很多书中可不多见。

sentences.en: So really love it, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很喜欢，你知道的。

sentences.en: Only the people who loved the Shogun TV series so much that they're now reading that novel are going to feel this thrill this year of reaching 1,000 pages.
sentences.zh: 只有那些因为太喜欢《幕府将军》电视剧而现在正在读原著小说的人，今年才能感受到这种读到1000页的快感。

sentences.en: But what's – so what's funny about this still is that, you know, for decades Moses has just sort of lived this way and sort of bulldozed over people metaphorically and literally.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，几十年来，摩西一直以这种方式生活，在隐喻和现实层面都横冲直撞。

sentences.en: And he still doesn't quite get that he's on the losing side of this.
sentences.zh: 而他仍然没意识到自己正处于劣势。

sentences.en: And so he takes off to Spain.
sentences.zh: 于是他动身去了西班牙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He leaves on a 24-day vacation to Spain.
sentences.zh: 他去西班牙度了24天的假。

sentences.en: This is one of those things where I kind of wonder sometimes – I trust Caro so much, but he'll be like, Moses was unstoppable.
sentences.zh: 这让我有时会感到疑惑——我非常信任卡罗，但他会说，摩西是不可阻挡的。

sentences.en: He always worked.
sentences.zh: 他总是工作。

sentences.en: Then he went on a vacation for two weeks in the Bahamas.
sentences.zh: 然后他去巴哈马度假了两周。

sentences.en: Like then he went on a two-week – 24-day vacation in Spain.
sentences.zh: 就像后来他又去西班牙度了24天的假。

sentences.en: And I'm like, I don't work as hard as Moses, and I don't take 24-day vacations in Spain.
sentences.zh: 我就想，我工作没摩西那么拼，我也没去西班牙度过24天的假。

sentences.en: You know, you were just in Spain, Roman, right?
sentences.zh: 你刚去过西班牙，对吧，罗曼？

sentences.en: You were not there for almost a month.
sentences.zh: 你没在那里待上近一个月吧。

sentences.en: I was not there for almost a month, but I definitely could have been.
sentences.zh: 我确实没待上近一个月，但我绝对可以待那么久。

sentences.en: That place is great.
sentences.zh: 那个地方太棒了。

sentences.en: Such a great country.
sentences.zh: 真是个伟大的国家。

sentences.en: It's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太美妙了。

sentences.en: I want to go back so badly.
sentences.zh: 我太想再去了。

sentences.en: I haven't been in years.
sentences.zh: 我已经好几年没去了。

sentences.en: It's so good.
sentences.zh: 真的太好了。

sentences.en: But you're right.
sentences.zh: 但你说得对。

sentences.en: He's so confident.
sentences.zh: 他太自信了。

sentences.en: He's like, I don't even need to be here.
sentences.zh: 他心想，我甚至不需要待在这里。

sentences.en: Unfortunately – and this will be a problem in the next chapter too – who does he leave in charge?
sentences.zh: 不幸的是——这在下一章也会是个问题——他把谁留下来负责了？

sentences.en: The mustache constable who is like Moses without the tact and the strategizing and the grace and the wit.
sentences.zh: 那个“胡子警官”，他就像没有圆滑手腕、没有战略眼光、没有风度和机智的摩西。

sentences.en: Constable is just unnecessarily over-stonewalling the press, and that keeps the story alive.
sentences.zh: 警官只是不必要地过度阻挠媒体，这反而让故事热度不减。

sentences.en: It makes the city angrier.
sentences.zh: 这让市民更加愤怒。

sentences.en: And Moses is not there to coordinate the responses of politicians, of park reps.
sentences.zh: 而摩西不在场，无法协调政客和公园代表们的应对措施。

sentences.en: The media is pouncing on and sensationalizing every little comment that someone makes to keep the story going.
sentences.zh: 媒体正在抓住每一个小评论进行炒作，以保持故事的持续发酵。

sentences.en: And the next round of judges in the court battle upholds the injunction.
sentences.zh: 法庭斗争的下一轮法官维持了禁令。

sentences.en: And one of them comments how he's happy with his judge's salary, but even for him, a stake at the tavern is pretty pricey.
sentences.zh: 其中一位法官评论说，他对自己的法官薪水很满意，但即便对他来说，在酒馆吃顿饭也太贵了。

sentences.en: You know, he can't afford to eat there regularly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他吃不起那里的常客餐。

sentences.en: And it starts getting safer to publicly criticize Moses.
sentences.zh: 公开批评摩西开始变得安全了。

sentences.en: This is a guy that people had to whisper about before if they wanted to criticize, but now it's becoming easier and easier to do that.
sentences.zh: 以前人们想批评他时还得窃窃私语，但现在这样做变得越来越容易了。

sentences.en: And Moses returns to the city after – that was probably an amazing vacation in Spain.
sentences.zh: 摩西从西班牙回来后——那次度假可能很棒。

sentences.en: It was harder to get news from overseas then, so like I'm sure he was shielded from some of this.
sentences.zh: 那时从海外获取新闻比较困难，所以我敢肯定他被屏蔽掉了一些消息。

sentences.en: And he tries to keep his cool, but he ends up blowing up in the press the way he always kind of used to when he was mad.
sentences.zh: 他试图保持冷静，但最终还是像以前生气时那样，在媒体面前爆发了。

sentences.en: And he goes so far as to attack Fanny Hurst, this respected elderly novelist, for making a stink about this children's play area when she doesn't even have children.
sentences.zh: 他甚至攻击了范妮·赫斯特，这位受人尊敬的老年小说家，因为她对这个儿童游乐区提出了质疑，而她自己甚至没有孩子。

sentences.en: How does she have a stake in this if she doesn't even have children?
sentences.zh: 如果她连孩子都没有，她怎么会关心这件事呢？

sentences.en: Which reading this, I was like, oh my god, I didn't think this part was going to be as relevant as it is now.
sentences.zh: 读到这里，我心想，天哪，我没想到这一部分在今天竟然如此切题。

sentences.en: It's really loathsome.
sentences.zh: 这真的很令人厌恶。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's really – the fact that it felt like it was ripped from today's headlines, this idea of someone saying, well, if you don't have children,
sentences.zh: 是的，这真的很……事实上，这感觉就像是从今天的新闻头条里摘出来的一样，这种观点认为：嗯，如果你没有孩子，

sentences.en: you don't have a stake in the country.
sentences.zh: 你就对这个国家没有利害关系。

sentences.en: You're somehow selfish, don't care about the future.
sentences.zh: 你就是某种自私的人，不关心未来。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's bonkers.
sentences.zh: 是的，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Unlike in the past, now the media is also giving the people Moses' attacks a chance to reply to his attacks.
sentences.zh: 与过去不同，现在媒体也给了那些被摩西攻击的人回击的机会。

sentences.en: And this attack on Fanny Hurst is really seen as too far.
sentences.zh: 而这次对范妮·赫斯特的攻击被认为太过分了。

sentences.en: You know what, I just realized I kept saying next chapter about Constable and the Mustache, but it's actually a chapter after next chapter.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，我刚意识到我一直说关于警官和“胡子”的是下一章，但其实是下下章。

sentences.en: That's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: My apologies.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Later in the episode.
sentences.zh: 在本集后面会提到。

sentences.en: And Moses realizes that if this case keeps going through the court, then there's going to be a discovery of other statements he's made, other sweetheart deals he's made.
sentences.zh: 摩西意识到，如果这个案子继续在法庭上审理，那么他发表过的其他言论、做过的其他“甜心交易”都会被披露出来。

sentences.en: He's going to have to testify about these things.
sentences.zh: 他将不得不就这些事情作证。

sentences.en: That would be bad.
sentences.zh: 那可就糟了。

sentences.en: He can't be in court testifying about this stuff because then he's on the record.
sentences.zh: 他不能出庭就这些事情作证，因为那样就会留下记录。

sentences.en: He can't play games about it.
sentences.zh: 他不能再玩弄手段了。

sentences.en: So he does what he almost never does.
sentences.zh: 所以他做了他几乎从不做的事。

sentences.en: He does something that is anathema to him.
sentences.zh: 他做了一件他深恶痛绝的事。

sentences.en: Rowan, what does he do in terms of building this parking lot?
sentences.zh: 罗曼，在建造这个停车场的问题上，他做了什么？

sentences.en: What does he do?
sentences.zh: 他做了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, he gives up.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他放弃了。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, I mean, it's kind of amazing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的，这真是太令人惊讶了。

sentences.en: Like, you know, he just, yeah, he doesn't go through with it, which is amazing.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，他只是，是的，他没有坚持到底，这太惊人了。

sentences.en: He just backs down.
sentences.zh: 他退缩了。

sentences.en: He does it.
sentences.zh: 他确实这么做了。

sentences.en: He tries to do it as quietly as possible.
sentences.zh: 他试图尽可能悄无声息地处理。

sentences.en: He has these delaying motions for the lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 他为诉讼提出了延期动议。

sentences.en: And then when the media dies down a little, he kind of agrees to give in so that it doesn't seem in his eyes as such a big loss.
sentences.zh: 然后当媒体热度稍微降下来时，他同意让步，这样在他看来就不算是一次重大的失败。

sentences.en: And he agrees to build a playground in that spot where the parking lot would have been.
sentences.zh: 他同意在原本打算建停车场的地方建一个游乐场。

sentences.en: And now, Rowan, I did a little on the ground investigating for this part of the episode.
sentences.zh: 现在，罗曼，我为这一集做了点实地调查。

sentences.en: Well, I was preparing for this episode.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在为这一集做准备时。

sentences.en: We had our event at the New York Historical Society where we talked to Robert Caro on stage.
sentences.zh: 我们在纽约历史学会举办了活动，在台上采访了罗伯特·卡罗。

sentences.en: It was amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: When people hear the audio from it, they will hear me noticeably run out of words.
sentences.zh: 当人们听到那段录音时，会听到我明显地语塞了。

sentences.en: I'm so emotional at the end of it.
sentences.zh: 最后我太激动了。

sentences.en: Like, I'm so, I was, when we were, it was an experience I'll carry with me in my heart for the rest of my life.
sentences.zh: 就像，我太……当我们……那是一段我余生都会铭记在心的经历。

sentences.en: But beforehand, I decided to do a little Caro-style investigating.
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，我决定做一点卡罗式的调查。

sentences.en: And I walked over to that part of the park because it's very close to the Historical Society.
sentences.zh: 我走到了公园的那一部分，因为它离历史学会很近。

sentences.en: And I wanted to be on the scene.
sentences.zh: 我想身临其境。

sentences.en: I said, what would Robert Caro do?
sentences.zh: 我说，罗伯特·卡罗会怎么做？

sentences.en: He would go and be in the space.
sentences.zh: 他会去现场，置身于那个空间。

sentences.en: And I walked around to those playgrounds that they put in, which are still there, which are definitely not as nice as a grove of trees would be.
sentences.zh: 我绕着他们建的那些游乐场走了一圈，它们现在还在那里，绝对没有一片树林那么好。

sentences.en: Like, they're okay.
sentences.zh: 它们还行吧。

sentences.en: They're okay playgrounds.
sentences.zh: 也就是普通的游乐场。

sentences.en: And I went down to Tavern on the Green.
sentences.zh: 然后我去了“绿地酒馆”。

sentences.en: And that parking circle is still there where cars can drop people off.
sentences.zh: 那个停车场环岛还在，汽车可以在那里让人下车。

sentences.en: And when you look at it, it feels like someone came along and took a bite out of the park and just left pavement behind.
sentences.zh: 当你看着它时，感觉就像有人走过来从公园里咬了一口，只留下了铺路石。

sentences.en: It really feels like the outside world of the city has invaded briefly and been pushed back but has left an emptiness, a void behind.
sentences.zh: 它确实让人感觉城市的外部世界短暂地入侵了这里，虽然被推了回去，但留下了一片空虚，一个空洞。

sentences.en: And so to imagine that parking lot in the area where those playgrounds are, it would have been a very noticeable chunk taken out of the park.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，在那些游乐场所在的地方建停车场，那将是从公园里挖走一块非常显眼的区域。

sentences.en: And it's an enormous park.
sentences.zh: 那是一个巨大的公园。

sentences.en: But walking around, you're like, yeah, this would have had an effect.
sentences.zh: 但走在周围，你会觉得，是的，这确实会产生影响。

sentences.en: It would have had a real effect on the people who lived in that neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 这对住在那个社区的人们会产生真正的影响。

sentences.en: And it feels like something would have been torn out of it.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像有什么东西被从里面撕裂了一样。

sentences.en: And for what?
sentences.zh: 为了什么？

sentences.en: For a parking lot?
sentences.zh: 为了一个停车场？

sentences.en: For a restaurant?
sentences.zh: 为了一家餐厅？

sentences.en: That is like – I looked at the prices on the menu and I was like, this is an overpriced restaurant.
sentences.zh: 这就像——我看了菜单上的价格，心想，这是一家定价过高的餐厅。

sentences.en: Like the prices have kept up with inflation, let's say.
sentences.zh: 价格跟上了通货膨胀，姑且这么说吧。

sentences.en: It's still an expensive hamburger.
sentences.zh: 那仍然是一个昂贵的汉堡。

sentences.en: So no thanks.
sentences.zh: 所以，不用了，谢谢。

sentences.en: That's what I say to that parking lot.
sentences.zh: 这就是我对那个停车场的看法。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's one of those things where he just kind of – there was a plan.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是那种情况，他只是……当时有一个计划。

sentences.en: He dug in.
sentences.zh: 他坚持己见。

sentences.en: He maybe had some friendly conversations with the proprietor of the restaurant or something like that to make it all make sense at the time.
sentences.zh: 他可能和餐厅老板进行了一些友好的交谈，或者类似的事情，让这一切在当时看起来都说得通。

sentences.en: But like it – I mean it's kind of amazing because this is not a thing to – like not a great hill to die on for him.
sentences.zh: 但它……我是说这真的很惊人，因为这根本不值得——对他来说，这并不是一个值得拼命去争取的阵地。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Like it doesn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 这简直毫无道理。

sentences.en: It's such a small thing.
sentences.zh: 这只是一件小事。

sentences.en: And what's notable is that at a certain point he perceived that as well because that's the new sort of behavior with him is he just realized like I – like there is no reason to take this much damage for this parking lot.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，在某个时刻他也意识到了这一点，因为他现在表现出一种新的行为模式，他意识到——比如，为了这个停车场而承受这么大的损失根本没有理由。

sentences.en: And it's chipped away at his reputation in a number of ways and it's such a tiny hill for this to happen on.
sentences.zh: 这在很多方面削弱了他的声誉，而且这仅仅是因为一件微不足道的小事。

sentences.en: But Moses' hope was nobody is going to notice that I gave in and lost this battle.
sentences.zh: 但摩西的希望是没人会注意到他妥协并输掉了这场战斗。

sentences.en: But it gets big media attention and Kara talks about the effect of that.
sentences.zh: 但这引起了媒体的广泛关注，卡拉谈到了这件事的影响。

sentences.en: He says the aura of infallibility was gone also.
sentences.zh: 他说那种不可战胜的光环也消失了。

sentences.en: He's talking about some other stuff that was gone.
sentences.zh: 他还在谈论其他一些消失的东西。

sentences.en: But the aura of infallibility was gone also.
sentences.zh: 但那种不可战胜的光环也消失了。

sentences.en: If Moses was the man who got things done, implicit was the assumption that the things that he got done were things that should be gotten done.
sentences.zh: 如果说摩西是一个能成事的人，那么隐含的假设就是他所做的事情都是应该做的事情。

sentences.en: He had always been portrayed as a man who was right.
sentences.zh: 他一直被塑造成一个永远正确的人。

sentences.en: But now in a single dramatic tableau, he had been shown to be utterly, unmistakably wrong.
sentences.zh: 但现在，在一幅戏剧性的画面中，他被证明是彻底的、毫无疑问的错误。

sentences.en: This idea that he's not a guy who can always get things done.
sentences.zh: 这种认为他不是一个总能成事的人的观点。

sentences.en: He's not a guy who is incorruptible.
sentences.zh: 他不是一个不可腐蚀的人。

sentences.en: Look at this sweetheart deal.
sentences.zh: 看看这笔诱人的交易。

sentences.en: And he's not infallible.
sentences.zh: 而且他并非不可战胜。

sentences.en: That he is not someone that you don't dare go up against because you're always going to lose.
sentences.zh: 他并不是那种让你不敢对抗，因为你总是会输的人。

sentences.en: All these things have been removed from his reputation by this, again, kind of a trivial thing that like to give a parking lot to a restaurant,
sentences.zh: 所有这些东西都因为这件事从他的声誉中被剥离了，再说一次，这只是一件琐碎的事情，比如给一家餐馆一个停车场，

sentences.en: which of all the things he's done is not – by far not the worSt.
sentences.zh: 在他所做的所有事情中，这绝不是最糟糕的。

sentences.en: And not something you would even expect him to stick so on.
sentences.zh: 而且这甚至不是你会期望他如此坚持的事情。

sentences.en: And you all kind of have to wonder, maybe if he hadn't gone on that vacation to Spain, he would have wriggled out of it in some more faith-saving way.
sentences.zh: 你们可能都会想，也许如果他没有去西班牙度假，他本可以用某种更保全颜面的方式摆脱困境。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: But what this does is it starts this cycle of fights in which Robert Moses does not win and also where Robert Moses is the bad guy.
sentences.zh: 但这样做开启了一系列罗伯特·摩西无法获胜的斗争，而且在这些斗争中，罗伯特·摩西成了反派。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And what's really notable is that there begins to be like a group of newspaper reporters who were not alive or at least sentient during those time periods where Robert Moses would destroy a newspaper man's life pretty easily.
sentences.zh: 真正值得注意的是，开始出现了一群报社记者，他们在罗伯特·摩西可以轻易摧毁报人生活的那个时期，要么还没出生，要么至少还没有感知能力。

sentences.en: And so they start seeing that there's some stories here and they start acting.
sentences.zh: 所以他们开始发现这里有一些故事，并开始采取行动。

sentences.en: And that's what the next chapter is about.
sentences.zh: 这就是下一章的内容。

sentences.en: It's called Late Arrival.
sentences.zh: 它叫《迟来的到来》。

sentences.en: We'll get to that after the break.
sentences.zh: 休息之后我们再谈这个。

sentences.en: So this is chapter 43, Late Arrival, which is like a little rude.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第43章，《迟来的到来》，这有点粗鲁。

sentences.en: Especially if Carol's like, I've been writing about this this whole time.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果卡罗尔说，我一直都在写这个。

sentences.en: What about you guys?
sentences.zh: 你们呢？

sentences.en: But I think he's talking about – I think he's not talking about the reporters who are focusing so much as the editors.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他谈论的——我认为他谈论的不是那些专注于报道的记者，而是编辑们。

sentences.en: Yeah, he really is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: The powers that be that run these newspapers.
sentences.zh: 那些经营这些报纸的当权者。

sentences.en: Finally, they start to see like that criticizing Moses and telling these stories that are very compelling to the news reading public is like, you know, it's worth it.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们开始意识到，批评摩西并讲述这些对新闻读者非常有吸引力的故事是值得的。

sentences.en: And it takes a lot of work to get them to that point.
sentences.zh: 要让他们达到这一点需要做很多工作。

sentences.en: And the work of a group of reporters that Carol really has a lot of fun writing about.
sentences.zh: 这是一群记者的工作，卡罗尔在写他们时真的很有乐趣。

sentences.en: I think he feels a real kinship with these characters and real – and admires them.
sentences.zh: 我认为他对这些角色有一种真正的亲近感，并且真的很钦佩他们。

sentences.en: He starts the chapter with an incredibly prescient quote from Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 他以罗伯特·摩西的一句极具预见性的话开始了这一章。

sentences.en: One of these quotes where it's like – it's super ironic.
sentences.zh: 其中一句引用是这样的——它超级讽刺。

sentences.en: So he makes use of it a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以他经常使用它。

sentences.en: It's from 1933 and Robert Moses is talking about another New York politician who was having his comeuppance.
sentences.zh: 它来自1933年，当时罗伯特·摩西正在谈论另一位正在遭受报应的纽约政客。

sentences.en: He says,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: The great statesman McKee is a synthetic character which never actually existed on sea or land, puffed up by the press, dot, dot, dot.
sentences.zh: 伟大的政治家麦基是一个从未在海上或陆地上真正存在过的合成人物，被媒体吹捧起来，点点点。

sentences.en: And now in the process of deflation, there is a large amount of unfairness to the individual in this process.
sentences.zh: 而现在在通货紧缩的过程中，这个过程对个人有很大的不公平。

sentences.en: But in the end, it arrives at the truth.
sentences.zh: 但最终，它会得出真相。

sentences.en: And it's like as if 25 or so years earlier, 23 years earlier, he's writing his own epitaph, you know, which is amazing.
sentences.zh: 这就像他在大约25年前，23年前，就在写他自己的墓志铭一样，你知道，这太神奇了。

sentences.en: It's very prescient.
sentences.zh: 非常有预见性。

sentences.en: It just happens sometimes, you know, history rhymes or whatever.
sentences.zh: 有时候就是会发生，你知道，历史总是惊人的相似之类的。

sentences.en: So we're introduced to some characters here.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在这里介绍了一些角色。

sentences.en: And one of them, one of the main ones here is this reporter for the World Telegram and Sun.
sentences.zh: 其中一个，这里的主要人物之一是《世界电讯太阳报》的记者。

sentences.en: Again, a newspaper that does not exist anymore.
sentences.zh: 同样，这是一份已经不存在的报纸。

sentences.en: And I always wonder if it's like did the Telegram newspaper and the Sun newspaper merge and then the World newspaper merged with that one?
sentences.zh: 我总是想知道，是不是《电讯报》和《太阳报》合并了，然后《世界报》又和那份报纸合并了？

sentences.en: A lot of these read like magnetic fridge poetry.
sentences.zh: 很多这些名字读起来就像冰箱上的磁力诗。

sentences.en: You know, there's there's like World Telegram, Herald, Times, you know, and then and then they just throw them up, rearrange them over time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有《世界电讯报》、《先驱报》、《时报》，你知道，然后他们就把它们扔上去，随着时间的推移重新排列。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I love it.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我喜欢它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so this reporter, Gene Gleason, he says to his editors,
sentences.zh: 所以这位记者吉恩·格里森对他的编辑说，

sentences.en: I want to investigate Robert Moses because I'm sure that there's other fishy stuff that the tavern on the green contract is not the only fishy thing about Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 我想调查罗伯特·摩西，因为我确信还有其他可疑的事情，绿地酒馆合同并不是罗伯特·摩西唯一可疑的事情。

sentences.en: And normally his editors would say no, but the Battle of Central Park has inspired them to say like, OK, I'll allow it.
sentences.zh: 通常他的编辑会拒绝，但中央公园之战激励了他们说，好吧，我批准了。

sentences.en: His editor says, I'll allow it.
sentences.zh: 他的编辑说，我批准了。

sentences.en: And Gleason wants to start investigating the power of public authorities.
sentences.zh: 格里森想开始调查公共当局的权力。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, no groundwork's been done on that story before because the records are inaccessible.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，之前没有为那个故事做任何基础工作，因为记录是无法获取的。

sentences.en: You can't get them.
sentences.zh: 你无法得到它们。

sentences.en: There's nowhere to start.
sentences.zh: 无从下手。

sentences.en: But a little groundwork has already been done on the Manhattan Town Public Housing Project.
sentences.zh: 但在曼哈顿镇公共住房项目上已经做了一些基础工作。

sentences.en: And so Gleason is like, OK, I think there's potential.
sentences.zh: 所以格里森觉得，好吧，我认为有潜力。

sentences.en: There's something for me to work off of.
sentences.zh: 我有东西可以利用。

sentences.en: And he starts working with one of the rewrite men at the newspaper.
sentences.zh: 他开始与报社的一名改稿员合作。

sentences.en: And I apologize to call him a rewrite man, but they're all all the reporters pretty much are men at this point.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉称他为改稿员，但此时几乎所有的记者都是男性。

sentences.en: The not again, not for fair reasons, not because the men were just doing such a bang up job reporting.
sentences.zh: 不是因为公平的原因，也不是因为男人们在报道方面做得特别出色。

sentences.en: And so he works with this rewriter, Fred J.
sentences.zh: 所以他与这位改稿员弗雷德·J·库克合作。

sentences.en: Cook.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里有趣的是，我忘记了报纸是如何以这种方式运作的，

sentences.en: And I think what's interesting here is I forget how a newspaper works in this way,
sentences.zh: 在办公室里，负责调查工作的人和负责实际撰写文章的人之间经常有这种能力的分工。

sentences.en: where there's often this delegation of abilities between the person who is out doing the investigative work.
sentences.zh: 他们在这方面合作得非常好。

sentences.en: And the person that you call it into at the office who does the actual kind of writing of the article.
sentences.zh: 但这只是提醒我，哦，他本可以——罗伯特·卡罗本可以写一整本关于报纸如何运作的书。

sentences.en: And they work together so well on this.
sentences.zh: 那将会非常迷人。

sentences.en: But it's a it's just a reminder to me of like, oh, he could have like Robert Carroll could have written a whole book about how newspapers work.
sentences.zh: 关于它我还有太多不知道的事情。

sentences.en: And it would have been fascinating.
sentences.zh: 但他们开始整理一系列文章，这些文章与其说是发现了新事物，不如说是第一次将所有关于曼哈顿镇的已知事实汇集在一起。

sentences.en: There's just so much I don't know about it.
sentences.zh: 事实表明，摩西的贫民窟清理计划正在清理功能正常的社区，并用虚无来取代它们，你知道，

sentences.en: But they start putting together a series of articles that don't discover new things so much as they assemble all the known facts about Manhattan Town in one place for the first time.
sentences.zh: 只是未完成的项目或贫民窟。

sentences.en: And the facts show that Moses's slum clearance program is clearing out functioning neighborhoods and replacing them with nothing, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们还没有发现该计划中的腐败。

sentences.en: just just unfinished projects or or sluMs.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实清楚地表明，该计划正在使住房状况恶化。

sentences.en: And they haven't found the corruption in the program yet.
sentences.zh: 它并没有改善这个问题。

sentences.en: But they do make it clear that the program is making housing worse.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，他们没有指责所谓的“城市”，而是点名摩西，并将责任归咎于他。

sentences.en: It is not improving the problem.
sentences.zh: 所以在电影里，这会是头版新闻。

sentences.en: And most importantly, rather than blaming the city in quotes, they name Moses and they put the blame on him.
sentences.zh: 它会破案。

sentences.en: And so in a movie, this would be front page news.
sentences.zh: 突然每个人都会调查摩西。

sentences.en: It would crack the case.
sentences.zh: 事情是这样吗，罗曼？

sentences.en: Suddenly everyone be investigating Moses.
sentences.zh: 不，根本不是那样。

sentences.en: Is that what happens, Roman?
sentences.zh: 这也是那种故事太复杂的事情之一，你知道。

sentences.en: No, that's that's not what happens at all.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's it's also one of those things where the story is just so complicated, you know.
sentences.zh: 它涉及许多不同的人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 也许那些人的受害经历对报纸读者来说并不那么引人注目。

sentences.en: And it involves lots of different people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这只是那种没有像这些公园斗争那样具有吸引力的事情之一，我的意思是，

sentences.en: And maybe those people, their their victimization isn't as compelling to newspaper readers.
sentences.zh: 因为我们下一章要谈论的另一个是另一种低风险的公园斗争。

sentences.en: You know, it's just one of those things that doesn't quite have the traction that that these sort of park fights do, which I mean,
sentences.zh: 但这是风险最低的公园斗争。

sentences.en: in the because the other one that we're going to talk about next chapter is another kind of low stakes park fight.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: But it's the lowest stakes park fight.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是因为误解，你知道，比其他任何事情都多。

sentences.en: It's incredible.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，这个故事并没有真正引起关注，因为它有所有这些东西的同样问题。

sentences.en: And it's basically over a misunderstanding, you know, more than anything else.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，这是他们揭露的一种非常经典的腐败，你知道，比如开发商挪用资金，然后故事就被掩盖了。

sentences.en: But, yeah, this one it's it's this one doesn't quite stick because it has the same kind of like issues of all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们就是不感兴趣。

sentences.en: But I mean, like this is a very classic corruption that they uncover, you know, like developers siphoned off money and then and the story just gets buried.
sentences.zh: 他们把它放在报纸的后页，编辑们仍然足够害怕摩西，以至于他们提前告诉了他。

sentences.en: You know, it just is not interesting to people.
sentences.zh: 他们还在报纸上为他提供了空间，让他进行反驳，攻击报纸自己的报道。

sentences.en: They put it on the back pages of the paper and the editors are still afraid enough of Moses that they tell him about it ahead of time.
sentences.zh: 而且他们没有把摩西的名字放在标题里。

sentences.en: And they provide space in the paper for him to, like, have a rebuttal where he attacks the paper's own story.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在现代变得更加熟悉的一件事是，人们通常只看标题。

sentences.en: And they don't put Moses name in the headlines.
sentences.zh: 他们不读文章。

sentences.en: And something that I think we've only become more familiar with in modern times is often people just look at the headlines.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·法洛斯写过这一点，标题以一种告诉读者主要信息是什么的方式构建故事。

sentences.en: They don't read the article.
sentences.zh: 所以标题可能与实际故事大相径庭，但标题是人们会记住的东西。

sentences.en: And the way you this is something that James Fallows writes about is that a headline frames a story in a way that tells the reader what the main information is.
sentences.zh: 所以如果摩西的名字不在标题里，人们就不会想到它。

sentences.en: And so the headline can be vastly unrepresentative of the actual story, but the headline is what's going to stick with people.
sentences.zh: 但一个故事引出另一个故事。

sentences.en: So if Moses name is not the headline, people are not going to think it.
sentences.zh: 卡罗谈到了这种多米诺骨牌效应，他说调查记者很快就会意识到他们职业的一种现象。

sentences.en: But one story leads to another.
sentences.zh: 当他们准备在新的领域写第一篇报道时，信息很难获得，但一旦第一篇报道见报，信息突然就变得丰富起来。

sentences.en: And Caro, there's this domino effect that Caro talks about where he says investigative reporters quickly become aware of a phenomenon of their profession.
sentences.zh: 每个城市机构都有不满者、理想主义者和不满的理想主义者，这是一个——我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: Information so hard to come by when they are preparing to write their first story in a new field suddenly becomes plentiful as soon as that first story has appeared in print.
sentences.zh: 这太像——这就像一个——这是一种很好的表达方式。

sentences.en: Every city agency has its malcontents and its idealists and its malcontent idealists, which is a – I love that.
sentences.zh: 官员、助手、职员和秘书们对机构的运作理念或内部进行的利益输送感到不满，他们多年来一直等待着某种可以表达他们感受的论坛的出现。

sentences.en: That is such like – that's like a – it's such a great way to say it.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦这些第一批文章出来，尽管它们在后面，格里森和库克的电话就开始响了。

sentences.en: Officials and aides and clerks and secretaries unhappy with the philosophy by which it is being run or the payoffs that are being made within it who have been just waiting for years for the appearance of some forum in which their feelings can be expressed.
sentences.zh: 人们纷纷站出来抱怨摩西。

sentences.en: And so once these first articles come out, even though they're in the back, Gleason and Cook's phones start ringing.
sentences.zh: 突然间，他们有了很多线索来继续这项调查并深入挖掘。

sentences.en: People are coming out of the woodwork to complain about Moses.
sentences.zh: 当然，每个人都害怕摩西，所以这一切都必须是非正式的。

sentences.en: And suddenly there are lots of leads for them to continue this investigation and dig deeper.
sentences.zh: 审计长办公室的一位消息人士揭露了开发商是如何从他们的住房开发项目中榨取数百万美元，同时让租户在没有暖气的情况下生活。

sentences.en: And, of course, everyone's afraid of Moses, so it all has to be off the record.
sentences.zh: 他们多年来没有向城市缴纳税款。

sentences.en: And a source in the comptroller's office reveals how the developers are milking their housing developments for millions while leaving tenants without heat.
sentences.zh: 而且，这些故事并没有得到太多的报道。

sentences.en: They're not paying taxes to the city for years.
sentences.zh: 它们在很多方面都很复杂。

sentences.en: And, again, these stories don't get that much play.
sentences.zh: 它们涉及名字和数字。

sentences.en: They're complicated in a lot of ways.
sentences.zh: 如果其他报纸提到它们，通常也只是为了刊登摩西的否认。

sentences.en: They involve names and numbers.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》仍然在为摩西效劳。

sentences.en: If other papers mention them, it's usually just to run Moses' denials.
sentences.zh: 就像他们还没准备好——他们对停车场有分歧，但他们还没准备好彻底背叛他。

sentences.en: And the New York Times is still carrying Moses' water for him.
sentences.zh: 然后在1957年6月，

sentences.en: Like they're still not ready – they disagreed about the parking lot, but they're not ready to turn on him completely.
sentences.zh: 消息传出，曼哈顿镇的开发商挪用了如此多的资金，以至于他们没有钱支付税款、抵押贷款，也没有钱建造他们签约建造的任何建筑。

sentences.en: And then in June 1957,
sentences.zh: 城市将不得不取消这个开发项目的赎回权。

sentences.en: it comes out that the Manhattan Town developers have siphoned off so much money that they have none left to pay their taxes or their mortgage or build any of the buildings they've contracted to build.
sentences.zh: 这是一个城市项目，交给了开发商，城市现在将不得不取消其赎回权。

sentences.en: And the city will have to foreclose on this development.
sentences.zh: 《时报》掩盖了这个故事，但其他报纸没有。

sentences.en: This is a city project that was given to developers the city will now have to foreclose on.
sentences.zh: 格里森让市长瓦格纳在新闻发布会上说，他被这些开发商欺骗了五年。

sentences.en: And the Times buries this story, but the other papers don't.
sentences.zh: 那是一件大事。

sentences.en: And Gleeson gets Mayor Wagner to say at a press conference that he was conned for five years by these developers.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: And that's a big thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是——这些新闻编辑室的基调正在发生很大变化。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 过去常批评一些质疑城市当权者的后起之秀的老记者，现在开始进行后续提问，询问——而且很明显，这种不同报纸的丰富多样性正在帮助改善现状。

sentences.en: I mean – and this is like the tone of these newsrooms is changing a lot.
sentences.zh: 就像他们——如果《时报》不报道，其他人也会报道。

sentences.en: And the older reporters who used to criticize some of these upstarts for questioning the powers that be in the city are now like doing follow-up questions where they ask – and it's beginning to become clear that this sort of rich diversity of different newspapers is helping the situation now.
sentences.zh: 因此，我的意思是，这确实是拥有一个活跃而充满活力的媒体的全部意义所在。

sentences.en: Like they're – if the Times isn't going to do it, someone else is going to cover it.
sentences.zh: 这真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: And therefore, like – I mean this is the whole point of having an active and vibrant press really.
sentences.zh: 格里森和库克再次沦为伟大的自由主义神话的牺牲品，即一旦你把信息发布出去，

sentences.en: It's kind of amazing.
sentences.zh: 系统就会发挥作用，人们会感到愤怒，或者他们会改变主意。

sentences.en: And Gleeson and Cook, once again, they fall prey to the great liberal myth that once you get the information out there,
sentences.zh: 那会很棒。

sentences.en: the system will do its job and people will get mad or they'll change their minds.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得，摩西现在要遭到报应了。

sentences.en: It'll be great.
sentences.zh: 这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: They're like, Moses is going to get his comeuppance now.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得，摩西现在要遭到报应了。

sentences.en: He's going to have his wings clipped by the mayor.
sentences.zh: 市长要削弱他的权力了。

sentences.en: But they don't understand how central Moses has become to the actual invisible machinery of the city.
sentences.zh: 但他们不明白，摩西已经成为这座城市隐形运作机制的核心。

sentences.en: And so Kara says, the two reporters' expectation was not unreasonable.
sentences.zh: 所以卡拉说，这两位记者的期望并非不合理。

sentences.en: Ordinarily, the tainting of a city program was scandal and failure.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，城市项目的腐败意味着丑闻和失败。

sentences.en: Scandal of immense proportions, failure five years in duration, would result in at least curtailment of the powers of the mayoral subordinate heading that program,
sentences.zh: 如此巨大的丑闻，长达五年的失败，至少会导致负责该项目的市长下属权力被削减，

sentences.en: lest the public outcry turn against the mayor.
sentences.zh: 以免公众的愤怒转向市长本人。

sentences.en: Their expectation was just based on a false premise that Robert Moses was really the mayor's subordinate.
sentences.zh: 他们的期望是基于一个错误的假设，即罗伯特·摩西真的是市长的下属。

sentences.en: They did not understand that as a matter of practical politics, the mayor could not discipline, demote, or remove Title I's administrator.
sentences.zh: 他们不明白，从实际政治角度来看，市长根本无法管教、降职或撤换“第一章”项目的负责人。

sentences.en: And so they were surprised at ensuing developments.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对随后的事态发展感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And those developments are that a spokesman of Moses' announces that new developers are coming in to take over Manhattan Town.
sentences.zh: 而事态的发展是，摩西的一位发言人宣布，新的开发商将接手曼哈顿城项目。

sentences.en: They're not going to have foreclosure hearings.
sentences.zh: 他们不会举行止赎听证会。

sentences.en: The old developers will have no penalties.
sentences.zh: 旧的开发商也不会受到任何惩罚。

sentences.en: In fact, the two principal stockholders of the mismanaged Manhattan Town, Inc.
sentences.zh: 事实上，管理不善的曼哈顿城公司（Manhattan Town, Inc.）的两名主要股东，

sentences.en: are going to be kept on the payroll as consultants.
sentences.zh: 还将作为顾问继续留在工资单上。

sentences.en: They're actually going to have their stock bought out from them, and they're going to remain stockholders in the new development.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上将获得股份回购，并且仍将是新开发项目的股东。

sentences.en: So these guys who cheated the city out of millions, they're going to keep making money off of it.
sentences.zh: 所以这些从城市骗走数百万美元的家伙，依然能从中继续赚钱。

sentences.en: And there's an outcry, and the mayor's like, all right, I'll take action.
sentences.zh: 于是引发了抗议，市长说，好吧，我会采取行动。

sentences.en: I will cut off some of the money those developers would receive.
sentences.zh: 我会削减这些开发商本应获得的部分资金。

sentences.en: They're still going to be rewarded for their failure.
sentences.zh: 他们依然会因为自己的失败而获得奖励。

sentences.en: They're just not getting as much reward.
sentences.zh: 只是得到的奖励没那么多了。

sentences.en: And Gleason Cook are like, we did all this work, and all we managed to do was get more money to the bad guys.
sentences.zh: 格里森和库克觉得，我们做了这么多工作，结果只是让坏人拿到了更多的钱。

sentences.en: And Moses has not really been affected at all.
sentences.zh: 而摩西实际上根本没受到任何影响。

sentences.en: And Moses has big plans at this point.
sentences.zh: 而且此时的摩西正有着宏大的计划。

sentences.en: He's planning this new vision of Manhattan's west side, Lincoln Center, which involves raising, not raising like raising up, but raising is like raising to the ground, you know,
sentences.zh: 他正在规划曼哈顿西区的新愿景——林肯中心，这涉及到“拆除”，不是那种“升起”，而是夷为平地，你知道的，

sentences.en: R-A-Z.
sentences.zh: R-A-Z（拆除）。

sentences.en: Like a razor, shaving.
sentences.zh: 就像剃刀，刮掉一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Oh, they probably come from the same group.
sentences.zh: 哦，它们可能来自同一个词根。

sentences.en: I never even thought about that.
sentences.zh: 我以前从没想过这一点。

sentences.en: Roman, you're so smart.
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你真聪明。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 别这样。

sentences.en: You're as smart as the empire that bears your name.
sentences.zh: 你和你名字所代表的帝国一样聪明。

sentences.en: They're going to raise 18 square blocks, and they're replacing them with Lincoln Center, the Metropolitan Opera, the New York Philharmonic, the New York Ballet,
sentences.zh: 他们要拆除18个街区，取而代之的是林肯中心、大都会歌剧院、纽约爱乐乐团、纽约芭蕾舞团，

sentences.en: the High School of Warming Arts, Juilliard, Fordham University's new campus.
sentences.zh: 表演艺术高中、茱莉亚学院、福特汉姆大学的新校区。

sentences.en: The newspapers are like, they love this plan.
sentences.zh: 报纸对此非常赞赏。

sentences.en: It's going to displace 7,000 low-income families and replace their homes with 4,000 luxury apartments, but the newspapers love it.
sentences.zh: 这将会导致7000户低收入家庭流离失所，并用4000套豪华公寓取代他们的家园，但报纸却对此大加赞赏。

sentences.en: And Roman, I want to hear you say, but then I have a thing I want to say about Lincoln Center.
sentences.zh: 罗曼，我想听你说，但我对林肯中心也有话要说。

sentences.en: Well, here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是这样的。

sentences.en: It's not better than 7,000 homes for people who can afford it, but Lincoln Center is pretty great.
sentences.zh: 它确实比不上7000个普通人的家，但林肯中心确实很棒。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That was what I was going to say.
sentences.zh: 这正是我要说的。

sentences.en: In all disclosure, I have spent so many memorable hours and beloved hours of my life at Lincoln Center.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，我在林肯中心度过了许多难忘且珍贵的时光。

sentences.en: Some of my happiest memories of experiencing culture and art have taken place there.
sentences.zh: 我人生中一些体验文化和艺术的最快乐记忆都发生在那里。

sentences.en: It's a place that is – it's inextricably tied in with my memories of my grandmother who I spent many, many hours with there.
sentences.zh: 那是一个与我祖母的记忆紧密相连的地方，我和她曾在那儿度过了许多许多时光。

sentences.en: And so it's – when I think about her, I think about Lincoln Center.
sentences.zh: 所以，每当我想到她，我就会想到林肯中心。

sentences.en: I was in New York for that event, and I walked by Lincoln Center twice, and each time I was just flooded with these feelings.
sentences.zh: 我当时在纽约参加那个活动，两次路过林肯中心，每次都让我感慨万千。

sentences.en: It's a really – it's a magical place.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个神奇的地方。

sentences.en: But again, you don't want to kick out 7,000 people for the opera.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，你确实不该为了歌剧院而赶走7000人。

sentences.en: Or if you do these big plants, you have to take care of them, and he never did that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你要搞这些大工程，你必须照顾好他们，而他从来没做过那种事。

sentences.en: But like, you know, you see movies in the park there in the summertime.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，夏天你可以在那儿看公园电影。

sentences.en: You know, like I've watched people dance to San Francisco's there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我曾在那儿看过人们跳旧金山风格的舞。

sentences.en: You know, like it's – and it has all these cultural – like as a center of culture, it's kind of stunning how concentrated it all is at this like place.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它作为文化中心，这种文化资源的集中程度简直令人震惊。

sentences.en: And anyway, it's just one of those ones like – I mean, Jones Beach didn't have anything that it was knocking down.
sentences.zh: 总之，它就是那种……我的意思是，琼斯海滩并没有拆掉任何东西。

sentences.en: So therefore, it's kind of this unalloyed, you know, good.
sentences.zh: 所以它算是一种纯粹的、你知道的，好事。

sentences.en: And this one, plenty alloyed, I guess.
sentences.zh: 而这个项目，我想，掺杂了太多东西。

sentences.en: But Lincoln Center is pretty awesome, I think.
sentences.zh: 但我认为林肯中心还是很棒的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's a – I mean, I feel a little about it like I felt like when I visited Versailles years ago where I was like,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我对此的感觉有点像我多年前参观凡尔赛宫时的感觉，当时我想，

sentences.en: they could have fed so many people with the money it took to build this house.
sentences.zh: 建造这座宫殿的钱本可以养活多少人啊。

sentences.en: But those people would still be dead now and the house is still here.
sentences.zh: 但那些人现在也已经不在了，而宫殿依然矗立在这里。

sentences.en: So like I wouldn't – I'm going to get to enjoy the house.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会……我还是会去享受这座宫殿。

sentences.en: Like that's – so it's – and like you're saying, the people that were displaced should have been taken care of, should have been accounted for,
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，那些流离失所的人本应得到照顾，本应被考虑到，

sentences.en: maybe should have had a say in the process.
sentences.zh: 也许本应在过程中有发言权。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: But it is hard not to feel as a New Yorker like a certain amount of pride in this – that there's this space where you can – I mean, if they were all scheduled on the same day,
sentences.zh: 但作为纽约人，很难不为这个空间感到某种自豪——我的意思是，如果它们都在同一天安排演出，

sentences.en: you could go to the opera, then go to the ballet, then hear the philharmonic, then look at the fountain where they shot that scene in the producers.
sentences.zh: 你可以去听歌剧，然后去看芭蕾，再听爱乐乐团，然后看看他们在《制片人》里拍摄过的那座喷泉。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: Like it's – there's – I've seen so many things there that were amazing.
sentences.zh: 我曾在那里看过很多精彩的演出。

sentences.en: It just – but it's hard to know that while you're there, so many people's homes were taken from them to make it possible.
sentences.zh: 只是，当你身处其中时，很难不去想，为了实现这一切，有多少人的家园被夺走了。

sentences.en: But you could argue – I mean, it's a little different, but it's sort of in the same philosophy that the existence of Central Park, even though it doesn't knock down homes,
sentences.zh: 但你可以争辩说——我的意思是，虽然有点不同，但这和中央公园存在的哲学是一样的，尽管它没有拆毁房屋，

sentences.en: its existence does deny a lot of spaces where homes could be built to make life more affordable in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 但它的存在确实占用了大量本可以建造住房的空间，从而让曼哈顿的生活成本变得更低。

sentences.en: And that's a choice that we make, and I think it's a good choice that is made on behalf of the citizens of New York.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我们做出的选择，我认为这是为了纽约市民而做出的正确选择。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's one of those things.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，这就是那种情况。

sentences.en: It does matter that there was something there ahead of time.
sentences.zh: 在它之前确实存在过别的东西，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: I'm not just being – I'm not trying to just like abstract this to the point of having just a philosophical discussion that where people mean nothing.
sentences.zh: 我不是在试图把问题抽象化到只进行哲学讨论，让人们变得毫无意义。

sentences.en: But there is a cost when it comes to like – you know, things take place in physical space.
sentences.zh: 但当涉及到……你知道，事情发生在物理空间中时，是有代价的。

sentences.en: And if you have one thing, you don't have another.
sentences.zh: 如果你拥有了一样东西，你就失去了另一样。

sentences.en: And this is one of those ones where at least the end product, I think, was executed in an interesting and valuable – like that was an interesting and valuable thing was made.
sentences.zh: 而这正是其中之一，至少我认为最终的产品执行得很有趣且有价值——创造出了有趣且有价值的东西。

sentences.en: I cannot say that about the Cross Bronx Expressway.
sentences.zh: 我无法对横跨布朗克斯高速公路（Cross Bronx Expressway）做出同样的评价。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: I certainly – I have no loving memories of the Cross Bronx Expressway at all.
sentences.zh: 我当然对横跨布朗克斯高速公路没有任何美好的回忆。

sentences.en: You know, whereas Lincoln Center is a place that, like I said, I have such a personal, you know, relationship with.
sentences.zh: 你知道，而林肯中心正如我所说，我和它有着非常私人的联系。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: I can't be impartial about it.
sentences.zh: 我无法对此保持公正。

sentences.en: But you're right that I think it gets to the heart of what so much of what Carol is saying, that everything is a choice.
sentences.zh: 但你是对的，我认为这触及了卡罗所说的大部分内容的核心，即一切都是选择。

sentences.en: Everything in governance and how you run a city is a choice.
sentences.zh: 治理和管理城市的一切都是一种选择。

sentences.en: And choosing to keep Central Park a park means effectively raising the price of housing for everyone who lives in the city a certain amount.
sentences.zh: 选择保留中央公园作为公园，实际上意味着提高了城市中每个人的住房成本。

sentences.en: And that was an easy choice to make when the city was half or not even a quarter built and you still had farm estates up in what would become, you know, 125th Street.
sentences.zh: 当城市只建了一半甚至不到四分之一，而你还在未来的125街拥有农场庄园时，这是一个容易做出的选择。

sentences.en: But it is a choice that they make and you're right that it's – there are those choices.
sentences.zh: 但这是他们做出的选择，你是对的，确实存在这些选择。

sentences.en: What is not the best way to do it though with Lincoln Center is the things that the papers didn't dig into in their enthusiasm for the news project.
sentences.zh: 不过，关于林肯中心，最糟糕的做法是报纸在对新项目的热情中没有深入挖掘的事情。

sentences.en: So how Moses is selling the land involved to developers at discount prices, how he's paying politically connected landowners like the Kennedys above market purchase prices.
sentences.zh: 比如摩西是如何以折扣价将土地卖给开发商的，他是如何向肯尼迪家族这样有政治背景的土地所有者支付高于市场价的收购费的。

sentences.en: I forgot about that.
sentences.zh: 我忘了那件事了。

sentences.en: And the administrator for Title I funds, Albert M.
sentences.zh: 而“第一章”资金的管理者阿尔伯特·M·科尔（Albert M. Cole），

sentences.en: Cole, he thinks this is the moment to demand Moses' answer for his kind of slipshod and misleading way of administering Title I projects.
sentences.zh: 他认为现在是时候要求摩西对他那种草率且误导性的“第一章”项目管理方式做出解释了。

sentences.en: And he threatens to cut off all of Title I's funds to the city if Moses doesn't change his ways and Moses threatens to resign.
sentences.zh: 他威胁说，如果摩西不改变做法，就切断城市所有的“第一章”资金，而摩西则威胁要辞职。

sentences.en: And within an hour, Mayor Wagner is backing him publicly.
sentences.zh: 不到一小时，瓦格纳市长就公开支持他了。

sentences.en: And the papers rush to back up Moses against the federal government just like when Roosevelt tried to get him fired.
sentences.zh: 报纸也像罗斯福试图解雇他时那样，争先恐后地支持摩西对抗联邦政府。

sentences.en: And Moses calls his powerful friends and they call the White House and Cole has to back down.
sentences.zh: 摩西给他的权贵朋友们打了电话，他们又打给白宫，科尔不得不退缩。

sentences.en: And Gleason and Cook, they start realizing Moses is still too powerful for the federal government to undercut him, let alone the city government, let alone regular people.
sentences.zh: 格里森和库克开始意识到，摩西的权力大到连联邦政府都无法削弱他，更不用说市政府或普通民众了。

sentences.en: And this aura of incorruptibility, even though it's not all the way there, it's still strong enough that people will defend him against the federal government.
sentences.zh: 这种“不可腐蚀”的光环，尽管并不完全属实，但依然强大到人们愿意为了他对抗联邦政府。

sentences.en: And his infallibility has been disproven by the Central Park battle.
sentences.zh: 虽然他的“绝对正确”在中央公园之战中已被证伪。

sentences.en: But there's still this idea that he is a public servant above politics.
sentences.zh: 但人们依然认为他是一位超越政治的公仆。

sentences.en: He's not on the take.
sentences.zh: 他不贪污。

sentences.en: He doesn't get involved in petty political battles.
sentences.zh: 他不参与琐碎的政治斗争。

sentences.en: And they realize it's going to take a lot more work on behalf of reporters whose editors have invested a lot of years in the Moses myth to make a real difference.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到，对于那些编辑们已经在“摩西神话”上投入了多年心血的记者来说，要产生真正的影响，还需要付出更多努力。

sentences.en: Moses has had such a relationship with top publishers, top editors, that he can just take it for granted that they are going to believe in him.
sentences.zh: 摩西与顶级出版商和编辑们有着深厚的关系，他可以理所当然地认为他们会相信他。

sentences.en: And Gleason and Cook find that their sources within city agencies after that first rush, they're newly paranoid.
sentences.zh: 格里森和库克发现，在最初的那阵冲动之后，他们在市政机构内的消息来源变得异常谨慎。

sentences.en: They don't want to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 他们不想谈论这件事。

sentences.en: But they keep digging, and they're able to start reporting the ties between local politicians and the slum clearance developers, developers who get contracts.
sentences.zh: 但他们继续挖掘，并开始报道当地政客与贫民窟清理开发商之间的联系，那些获得合同的开发商。

sentences.en: And by 1958, they can show that William S.
sentences.zh: 到1958年，他们能够证明威廉·S·利伯瓦尔德（William S. Lieberwald），

sentences.en: Lieberwald, the director of Moses' slum clearance committee, is a stockholder in the Nassau Management Company,
sentences.zh: 摩西贫民窟清理委员会的主任，是拿骚管理公司（Nassau Management Company）的股东，

sentences.en: the real estate relocation firm that we talked about in a previous episode that has been paid millions to do essentially nothing, to help nobody.
sentences.zh: 就是我们在上一集提到的那家房地产搬迁公司，它拿了数百万美元却基本什么都没做，没帮到任何人。

sentences.en: And they start finding more and more links between Moses' people and the companies being given contracts and local politicians.
sentences.zh: 他们开始发现摩西的人、获得合同的公司以及当地政客之间越来越多的联系。

sentences.en: But at this point, Roman, you talked about how, like, other reporters are going to jump in.
sentences.zh: 但此时，罗曼，你谈到其他记者会加入进来，

sentences.en: They're still not jumping in yet.
sentences.zh: 他们还没有加入。

sentences.en: Editors keep removing Moses' names from their articles.
sentences.zh: 编辑们不断从他们的文章中删掉摩西的名字。

sentences.en: They keep pressuring them, do some other stories.
sentences.zh: 他们不断向他们施压，让他们去写别的故事。

sentences.en: These aren't too complicated.
sentences.zh: 这些并不太复杂。

sentences.en: And Caro says, the stories about corruption in these projects are being put on page 27.
sentences.zh: 卡罗说，关于这些项目腐败的故事被放在了第27页。

sentences.en: And the stories about how Moses has this great project he's building are on page 1.
sentences.zh: 而关于摩西正在建设的伟大项目的故事则在第1页。

sentences.en: And by 1959, the leads are really drying up.
sentences.zh: 到了1959年，线索真的枯竭了。

sentences.en: Moses is starting to get public works named after him, which is pretty out of the ordinary for a living person.
sentences.zh: 摩西开始以自己的名字命名公共工程，这对于一个在世的人来说是非常不寻常的。

sentences.en: And Gleason and Cook, they're like, we were going to pin him on Title I, on the corruption, but I guess that's dead now, until they come up with their plan.
sentences.zh: 格里森和库克觉得，我们本想在“第一章”项目和腐败问题上抓住他，但我想现在没戏了，直到他们想出了新计划。

sentences.en: And Caro says, to understand what Gleason and Cook did then, it is necessary to understand Gleason and Cook.
sentences.zh: 卡罗说，要理解格里森和库克当时做了什么，就必须理解格里森和库克本人。

sentences.en: And you're like, I've been reading about these guys.
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，我一直在读关于这些人的内容。

sentences.en: Now's when you're going to tell me about them?
sentences.zh: 现在你才要告诉我关于他们的事？

sentences.en: And he just gives – he gets into their personalities.
sentences.zh: 他只是深入探讨了他们的性格。

sentences.en: But he's Gleason, he's that classic front page, you know, His Girl Friday, hard-drinking, fast-talking reporter, dedicated to protecting the little guy, loves the thrill of it,
sentences.zh: 格里森是那种经典的头版记者，你知道的，就像《小报妙冤家》里那样，酗酒、快言快语，致力于保护小人物，热爱那种刺激感，

sentences.en: the rush.
sentences.zh: 那种冲劲。

sentences.en: And Cook is this unassuming guy, but he's also a crusading liberal who wants to protect the little guy.
sentences.zh: 而库克是一个谦逊的人，但他也是一个想要保护小人物的激进自由派。

sentences.en: And Caro mentions how Cook wrote a book defending Alger Hiss when Alger Hiss was at his most priesh, a stance that in 1974 seemed better.
sentences.zh: 卡罗提到库克曾写过一本书为阿尔杰·希斯（Alger Hiss）辩护，当时正是希斯最受争议的时候，这种立场在1974年看起来似乎更好。

sentences.en: That it has aged poorly now, considering Alger Hiss – I don't want to reopen it, but he probably did what he was accused of doing, you know.
sentences.zh: 现在看来已经过时了，考虑到阿尔杰·希斯——我不想重提旧事，但他很可能确实做了他被指控做的事，你知道的。

sentences.en: It is no longer a just taken for granted that if you're liberal, you love Alger Hiss and want to defend him.
sentences.zh: 现在已经不再理所当然地认为，如果你是自由派，你就会爱阿尔杰·希斯并想为他辩护。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And for anyone listening who doesn't know that name, either look it up or don't worry about it.
sentences.zh: 对于任何不知道这个名字的听众，要么去查一下，要么不用管它。

sentences.en: It's the kind of thing that, like, my grandparents took as – just as took as gospel, that Alger Hiss had been railroaded, you know.
sentences.zh: 这就像是我祖父母辈奉为圭臬的事情，认为阿尔杰·希斯是被冤枉的，你知道的。

sentences.en: And Cook hates that Moses pushes people around, and Caro quotes him using the phrase the power brokers to talk about Moses and the people around him,
sentences.zh: 库克讨厌摩西欺压他人，卡罗引用他使用“权力掮客”（the power brokers）这个词来形容摩西及其周围的人，

sentences.en: which is I think the first time the phrase really gets brought up in the mouth of somebody.
sentences.zh: 我想这是这个词第一次真正从某人口中说出来。

sentences.en: You know, maybe this is around the time it's getting born.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许这就是它诞生的时期。

sentences.en: I actually kind of wondered if this is where Caro gets the name of the book, like, because this is all reported, you know, obviously well before he's writing all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我其实有点好奇这是否就是卡罗书名的由来，因为这一切报道显然远在他写这些东西之前。

sentences.en: And if this is unlocking – I don't know.
sentences.zh: 如果这是一种启发——我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: The power broker is not a phrase I know besides coming from this book, really.
sentences.zh: 除了这本书，我真的不知道“权力掮客”这个词。

sentences.en: I mean –
sentences.zh: 我的意思是——

sentences.en: I know it from this book, and I know it from the Marvel Comics super villain, the power broker, who's the guy who gives people superpowers.
sentences.zh: 我是从这本书里知道的，也从漫威漫画里的超级反派“权力掮客”那里知道的，就是那个赋予人们超能力的人。

sentences.en: Superpowers, yeah.
sentences.zh: 超能力，是的。

sentences.en: But it seems to me like it's possible that – I mean, maybe it's just sort of like common parlance among people who write about politics and stuff,
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，这很有可能——我的意思是，也许这只是政治评论者之间的一种常用语，

sentences.en: that there are power brokers and this and that.
sentences.zh: 说有权力掮客之类的。

sentences.en: And maybe it's just such super common of a phrase.
sentences.zh: 也许这只是一个非常通用的词汇。

sentences.en: But it shows up here, and it's very notable to me.
sentences.zh: 但这出现在这里，对我来说非常引人注目。

sentences.en: You know, like this is sort of a great moment in the book.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这在书中算是一个很棒的时刻。

sentences.en: It is the moment in the movie where someone says the title, oh, he's like some kind of power broker.
sentences.zh: 这是电影里有人说出片名的时刻，哦，他就像某种权力掮客。

sentences.en: And the audience goes, oh.
sentences.zh: 然后观众会说，哦。

sentences.en: And we've heard it from – we've heard the phrase used by Caro, but we haven't used – we haven't heard it used by a character in the story, you know, which is really great.
sentences.zh: 我们从卡罗那里听到过这个说法，但我们还没听到故事里的角色用过这个词，你知道，这真的很棒。

sentences.en: But he doesn't make a lot out of it.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有过多渲染这一点。

sentences.en: You know, he just has it in the quote.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他只是把它写在引语里。

sentences.en: And it's – so it's done very subtly.
sentences.zh: 所以，这处理得非常微妙。

sentences.en: And so Gleason Cook, the thing that he talks about here also is that they're competitive.
sentences.zh: 格里森·库克在这里谈到的另一件事是，他们之间存在竞争。

sentences.en: All these reporters are competitive.
sentences.zh: 所有的记者都在竞争。

sentences.en: They want the credit.
sentences.zh: 他们想要功劳。

sentences.en: They want the glory of the big story.
sentences.zh: 他们想要大新闻带来的荣耀。

sentences.en: They want to beat the other papers.
sentences.zh: 他们想要打败其他报社。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: But they realize if their editors aren't supporting them, they're going to have to find a way around that.
sentences.zh: 但他们意识到，如果编辑不支持他们，他们就得想办法绕过这一关。

sentences.en: And the only way around that is to start colluding with the ultimate enemy, other reporters at other papers.
sentences.zh: 而唯一的办法就是开始与终极敌人——其他报社的记者——勾结。

sentences.en: And this is what I was hinting at earlier is this – I love this so much.
sentences.zh: 这就是我之前暗示的——我太喜欢这一点了。

sentences.en: Like this is the whole part – I mean this is the best part of this chapter, which is essentially them coming to the conclusion that, well,
sentences.zh: 这整段——我是说这是这一章最精彩的部分，本质上是他们得出了一个结论，那就是，

sentences.en: if every – if editor is going to bury it here, I can tip off this other person and we can begin to sort of trade parts of these stories.
sentences.zh: 如果编辑要把新闻压下来，我可以给另一个人通风报信，我们就可以开始交换这些报道的部分内容。

sentences.en: And they actually kind of – I mean they really do collude.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上——我是说他们确实在勾结。

sentences.en: Like it's not just sort of like kind of allowing it to happen.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是顺其自然。

sentences.en: Like they meet and decide what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 他们会面并决定接下来该怎么做。

sentences.en: Yeah, they're meeting in bars and saying, you take this part of the story and then after you run that, I'll do this part.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们在酒吧里碰头，说，你负责报道这部分，等你发了之后，我再做那部分。

sentences.en: Okay, and then you take this tip and you handle that.
sentences.zh: 好的，然后你拿这个线索，你去处理那个。

sentences.en: They are – I mean it's like insider trading between reporters.
sentences.zh: 他们——我是说这就像记者之间的内幕交易。

sentences.en: But in a way that is – there's nothing legal about it and it helps them, you know.
sentences.zh: 但从某种程度上说——这完全不合法，但这对他们有帮助，你知道的。

sentences.en: And Caro every now and then he'll indulge in a very – in a kind of fanciful metaphor or description.
sentences.zh: 卡罗偶尔会沉溺于一种非常——一种异想天开的隐喻或描述中。

sentences.en: And he has one here and he just says, soon like two flamenco dancers spurring each other to wilder and wilder efforts,
sentences.zh: 他这里就有一处，他只是说，就像两个弗拉门戈舞者互相激励，做出越来越狂野的动作，

sentences.en: Hadad and Gleeson were both helping and striving to outdo each other.
sentences.zh: 哈达德和格里森都在互相帮助，努力超越对方。

sentences.en: Their stories picking up and taking off from each other's and hitting harder and harder.
sentences.zh: 他们的报道相互衔接、借力，冲击力越来越强。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: I just love that I'm comparing them to two flamenco dancers, you know, challenging each other.
sentences.zh: 我就是喜欢他把他们比作两个互相挑战的弗拉门戈舞者，你知道的。

sentences.en: And they know that if their editors see a story about Title I corruption in another paper, they're going to want them to get on it.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，如果编辑看到另一家报纸报道了第一章的腐败问题，他们也会想要跟进。

sentences.en: It's like, you know, they're bringing the spice back into the relationship between their editors and this story by cheating with another paper, you know.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，他们通过与其他报纸“出轨”，重新为编辑和这篇报道之间的关系注入了活力，你知道的。

sentences.en: And soon there's this circle of reporters that are trading tips and things to strategizing how to get this done.
sentences.zh: 很快就形成了一个记者圈子，他们交换线索，策划如何完成报道。

sentences.en: And Caro says about these reporters, like you said, Roman, earlier, these are young people.
sentences.zh: 卡罗在谈到这些记者时说，就像你刚才说的，罗曼，这些人都是年轻人。

sentences.en: They're mostly in their 20s and 30s.
sentences.zh: 他们大多在二三十岁。

sentences.en: They're young enough that they are still idealistic.
sentences.zh: 他们足够年轻，依然怀有理想主义。

sentences.en: And they're also young enough that the Moses myth does not matter to them.
sentences.zh: 而且他们也足够年轻，摩西的神话对他们来说毫无意义。

sentences.en: They were babies when Jones Beach got built.
sentences.zh: 琼斯海滩建成时，他们还是婴儿。

sentences.en: They don't remember him as the hero of the working class and the liberal reformers.
sentences.zh: 他们不记得他是工人阶级和自由改革派的英雄。

sentences.en: They know him as an old man, this stubborn old dictator who needs to be toppled.
sentences.zh: 他们眼中的他是一个老头，一个必须被推翻的顽固独裁者。

sentences.en: And they're also too young to remember or have felt the threat of Moses ending your career when his bloodhounds go after you.
sentences.zh: 而且他们也太年轻了，不记得或没感受过摩西的走狗追杀你时，他能终结你职业生涯的威胁。

sentences.en: They are fearlessly young and they're also like in the way that can help a young person kind of ignorant of history or the feeling of history in that what Moses means to them is what Moses is right now and not what he used to be.

sentences.en: Don't care.
