sentences.zh: 而实际上这似乎是一场摩西并不想要、也没胃口打下去，最终放弃了的斗争，

sentences.en: but it still hurt his reputation so badly.
sentences.zh: 但这仍然严重损害了他的声誉。

sentences.en: And it seems like comparing that quote from earlier from Moses, it's unfair, but it gets out of truth.
sentences.zh: 这似乎印证了摩西之前的那句名言，虽然不公平，但却触及了真相。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Because if ever there was a thing to get Moses on, it's not this one.
sentences.zh: 因为如果说有什么事能抓住摩西的把柄，那绝不是这一件。

sentences.en: And so Moses, he's always been a fan of Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 摩西一直都是莎士比亚的粉丝。

sentences.en: He wrote poetry in college.
sentences.zh: 他在大学时还写过诗。

sentences.en: You know he loves Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 你知道他热爱莎士比亚。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 得了吧。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in 1956, Joseph Papp, he's a young theater impresario, he says to Moses,
sentences.zh: 1956年，年轻的戏剧经纪人约瑟夫·帕普对摩西说，

sentences.en: can I put on free Shakespeare plays in this amphitheater on the Lower East Side that the Parks Department built?
sentences.zh: 我能在下东区公园管理局建的那个露天剧场免费上演莎士比亚戏剧吗？

sentences.en: And that Moses built in part because Al Smith had told Moses,
sentences.zh: 而那个剧场是摩西建的，部分原因是阿尔·史密斯曾对摩西说，

sentences.en: when I was young, I could not afford tickets to the theater.
sentences.zh: 我年轻的时候，买不起戏票。

sentences.en: I just couldn't afford to go.
sentences.zh: 我就是看不起戏。

sentences.en: And Moses seems to admire Papp's genuine interest in providing shows for free.
sentences.zh: 摩西似乎很欣赏帕普想要免费提供演出的真诚兴趣。

sentences.en: And besides, the stage is empty all the time anyway.
sentences.zh: 况且，那个舞台反正一直空着。

sentences.en: No one does anything with it.
sentences.zh: 没人用它。

sentences.en: So why not?
sentences.zh: 所以为什么不呢？

sentences.en: And Papp starts putting on productions there, and they're very respected.
sentences.zh: 于是帕普开始在那里制作演出，而且非常受人尊敬。

sentences.en: The local audiences who cannot afford theater tickets love them.
sentences.zh: 买不起戏票的当地观众非常喜欢这些演出。

sentences.en: And this happens throughout history with live theater, but especially with Shakespeare,
sentences.zh: 这种情况在现场戏剧史上屡见不鲜，尤其是莎士比亚戏剧，

sentences.en: is that you show them to people who you think are going to be like,
sentences.zh: 就是你把它们展示给那些你以为会觉得，

sentences.en: this is too complicated.
sentences.zh: 这太复杂了，

sentences.en: I don't understand it.
sentences.zh: 我看不懂的人看，

sentences.en: And they love it.
sentences.zh: 结果他们却爱上了它。

sentences.en: Like in the Old West, Shakespeare was incredibly popular.
sentences.zh: 就像在旧西部，莎士比亚就非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: Like it's just, it's writing that just gets to, you know,
sentences.zh: 这只是，这些文字直抵人心，你知道，

sentences.en: he's almost Robert Carrow-esque in his ability to put words together, you know.
sentences.zh: 他在遣词造句的能力上几乎和罗伯特·卡罗如出一辙，你知道的。

sentences.en: And Papp is like, I want to expand these shows.
sentences.zh: 帕普说，我想扩大这些演出规模。

sentences.en: I want to put them in more parks.
sentences.zh: 我想在更多的公园里上演。

sentences.en: And there's one person standing in his way.
sentences.zh: 但有一个人挡了他的路。

sentences.en: Moses gives permission, but there's one person who doesn't like it.
sentences.zh: 摩西准许了，但有一个人不喜欢。

sentences.en: Stuart Constable, the mustache.
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特·康斯特布尔，那个留胡子的家伙。

sentences.en: Who we already know is a foe of mothers, doesn't like moms, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们已经知道他是母亲们的死敌，不喜欢妈妈们，你知道的。

sentences.en: There is a kind of like strain in these chapters of subordinates to Moses who don't have any of his skill whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 在这些章节中，摩西的下属们似乎有一种共同的特点，就是他们完全没有摩西那样的本事。

sentences.en: Like they're as pugnacious as he is, but, but can't like operate around people, can't like bully people the same way and make wrongheaded decisions that, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们像他一样好斗，但却无法像他那样处理人际关系，无法像他那样欺压他人，反而做出了错误的决定，你知道，

sentences.en: to his credit in a way, Robert Moses has great loyalties to his subordinates.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，罗伯特·摩西对下属的忠诚值得称赞。

sentences.en: But they just don't deserve it because they are kind of so boneheaded so much of the time.
sentences.zh: 但他们根本不配，因为他们大部分时间都太固执了。

sentences.en: Yeah, you see it a lot in organizations where someone at the top has a special quality that has allowed them to create this position of power.
sentences.zh: 没错，你在很多组织里都能看到这种情况，高层的人拥有某种特殊品质，使他们能够创造出这种权力地位。

sentences.en: And then, yeah, the people underneath them try to imitate that or have been taught to work in that ethic and they just don't have it.
sentences.zh: 然后，手下的人试图模仿这种品质，或者被教导要遵循这种职业道德，但他们就是没有那种能力。

sentences.en: You know, they just don't, they can't do it the right way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们就是做不到，无法以正确的方式行事。

sentences.en: And, and we'll see as we get through it, yeah, his loyalty to his subordinates, which would normally be a, a positive thing, gets him into so much trouble here.
sentences.zh: 而且，随着我们深入了解，你会发现，他对下属的忠诚，这本该是一件积极的事情，却让他陷入了巨大的麻烦。

sentences.en: And this whole chapter has an element of farce about it, you know, there's, there's, it's, it's written with a kind of like almost the most winking that Caro gets throughout.
sentences.zh: 整个这一章有一种闹剧的成分，你知道，它是用一种近乎卡罗全书中最戏谑的笔调写成的。

sentences.en: And it's, it's a, it's a fun chapter, but it's, I have, this is the chapter I maybe have the most trouble with in some ways.
sentences.zh: 这是一章很有趣的内容，但在某些方面，这可能是我读起来最费劲的一章。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we'll talk about it.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我们以后再聊。

sentences.en: We'll talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我们会聊到的。

sentences.en: I'm reading it each time I've read it where I'm like, why is this jamper in the book?
sentences.zh: 我每次读的时候都在想，为什么这一章会出现在书里？

sentences.en: Like, well, there's nothing about James Jacobs, but there's all this stuff about Joe Pap and Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 比如，这里面完全没有关于简·雅各布的内容，全是关于乔·帕普和莎士比亚的事。

sentences.en: But, but I think he's, it's because this larger point I think he's getting to.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这是因为他想要表达一个更宏大的观点。

sentences.en: But Pap proposes putting on plays in Central Park.
sentences.zh: 帕普提议在中央公园上演戏剧。

sentences.en: And Moses is like, that's okay if you don't charge admission for them.
sentences.zh: 摩西说，只要不收门票就行。

sentences.en: And this is a start of Shakespeare in the Park, which again is for the cultural life of New York City is one of, by this point in the year 2024,
sentences.zh: 这就是“公园里的莎士比亚”的开端，对于纽约市的文化生活来说，到了2024年的今天，

sentences.en: one of the most beloved things going on in New York.
sentences.zh: 这已成为纽约最受欢迎的活动之一。

sentences.en: And I have seen shows in that festival.
sentences.zh: 我也看过那个艺术节的演出。

sentences.en: Festival, I know, like friends of mine, I couldn't do this because I had a job, but friends of mine would go, they would wait online for hours.
sentences.zh: 艺术节，我知道，我的朋友们，因为我有工作没法去，但我的朋友们会去，他们会排几个小时的队。

sentences.en: Because all you need to do is wait online.
sentences.zh: 因为你只需要排队就行了。

sentences.en: You'd wait online for hours.
sentences.zh: 你会排上几个小时的队。

sentences.en: And like, I remember my friend being like, oh yeah, I was standing next to Mike Myers waiting for Shakespeare in the Park tickets for four hours.
sentences.zh: 我记得我朋友说，哦，是的，我当时站在迈克·梅尔斯旁边，排了四个小时的队买“公园里的莎士比亚”的票。

sentences.en: You know, like that's just what you do.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是你要做的事。

sentences.en: And it's first come, first serve.
sentences.zh: 而且是先到先得。

sentences.en: And it's just a, it's just a beloved event to a certain section of New Yorkers.
sentences.zh: 对于一部分纽约人来说，这是一个备受喜爱的活动。

sentences.en: And it's kind of magical when you are in the park, how Central Park, even it's a safe park, but now, but it's still scary to be in a park at night.
sentences.zh: 当你身处公园时，那种感觉很神奇，中央公园虽然是个安全的公园，但晚上待在公园里还是很吓人。

sentences.en: You know, it's like you're in the woods, it's scary.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像在树林里一样，很可怕。

sentences.en: And you've been raised on these stories of people being killed in the park, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且你从小听多了在公园里被人杀害的故事，你知道的。

sentences.en: But there's something magical about how when there's a large group of people seeing a performance, because I used to see the Philharmonic in the park quite a bit too.
sentences.zh: 但当一大群人聚在一起观看演出时，有一种神奇的感觉，因为我以前也经常去公园看爱乐乐团的演出。

sentences.en: It transforms that space, and it takes a space that could be threatening and turns into this communal space that is magical and warm and what a city does best, you know,
sentences.zh: 它改变了那个空间，把一个可能令人不安的地方变成了一个神奇、温暖的公共空间，这正是城市最擅长做的事情，你知道，

sentences.en: which is take the fear of solitude and turn it into a shared experience with lots of strangers who become your neighbors.
sentences.zh: 那就是把孤独的恐惧转化为与许多陌生人共享的体验，让他们成为你的邻居。

sentences.en: You know, they become people that you know for a moment and have a connection to that otherwise would just be, you know, unknown names, unknown faces, unknown lives.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们成为了你暂时认识并产生联系的人，否则他们只会是未知的名字、未知的面孔、未知的人生。

sentences.en: It's just there's something very magical about it.
sentences.zh: 这其中确实有一种非常神奇的东西。

sentences.en: But, and Moses, to his credit, likes this.
sentences.zh: 但是，摩西值得称赞的一点是，他喜欢这个。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, he thinks it's great.
sentences.zh: 是的，他不，他觉得这很棒。

sentences.en: This is what, he, this is the sort of, like, he, he's not a big fan of, like, just wild glens and trees and stuff, but this is the type of thing that he is into.
sentences.zh: 这就是他，他不太喜欢那种荒野、树木之类的东西，但这正是他感兴趣的那种事情。

sentences.en: Yes, you are using a space.
sentences.zh: 是的，你在利用一个空间。

sentences.en: He does not like unused space.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢闲置的空间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And so if you can use it and use it for something that no one else is doing with it, it's, he's for it.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你能利用它，而且是用于别人没做过的事情，他就会支持。

sentences.en: And he really appreciates the chutzpah that Joe Papp has in the way he fundraises for it.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常欣赏乔·帕普在筹款方式上的那种胆识。

sentences.en: And Moses comes to see him, the book implies, as kind of like a young go-getter like himself who has a project that's to help people and will go to any length to do it.
sentences.zh: 书中暗示，摩西把帕普看作是像他自己一样的年轻进取者，有一个帮助他人的项目，并且会不惜一切代价去实现它。

sentences.en: And so by 1959, Moses, they've never met each other, but Moses is telling Joe Papp, I'll handle the fundraising for another season of plays in the park.
sentences.zh: 到了1959年，摩西，虽然他们从未见过面，但摩西告诉乔·帕普，我会负责下一季公园演出的筹款。

sentences.en: I'll take care of it.
sentences.zh: 我会搞定的。

sentences.en: I like what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢你做的事。

sentences.en: Don't worry about money.
sentences.zh: 别担心钱的问题。

sentences.en: And then he leaves town on a three-week vacation of Barbados, another one of these long vacations that this workaholic is taking, you know.
sentences.zh: 然后他去巴巴多斯度了三周的假，又是这个工作狂长假中的一次，你知道。

sentences.en: Maybe he's taking more of them at this age.
sentences.zh: 也许他这个年纪休假更多了。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, he leaves things in the hands of the mustache, Constable, who does not like Shakespeare, doesn't trust Papp.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，他把事情交给了那个留胡子的康斯特布尔，他不喜欢莎士比亚，也不信任帕普。

sentences.en: And it only gets worse when he learns that Papp refused to name names before HUAC because Constable is, if anything, just a straightforward anti-communist, you know,
sentences.zh: 当他得知帕普拒绝在HUAC面前供出名单时，情况变得更糟了，因为康斯特布尔充其量只是一个直截了当的反共分子，你知道，

sentences.en: steak and potatoes, New York guy with a big mustache.
sentences.zh: 一个留着大胡子、朴实无华的纽约人。

sentences.en: Later on, reporters are like, doesn't this smack of McCarthyism?
sentences.zh: 后来，记者问他，这难道没有麦卡锡主义的嫌疑吗？

sentences.en: And he goes, what's wrong with McCarthy?
sentences.zh: 他说，麦卡锡有什么错？

sentences.en: And that kind of says everything you need to know about the mustache.
sentences.zh: 这句话几乎道出了关于那个留胡子家伙的一切。

sentences.en: And so what, you know, what the constable, or not the constable, I guess, the mustache constable.
sentences.zh: 所以，那个康斯特布尔，或者不是康斯特布尔，我想，是那个留胡子的康斯特布尔。

sentences.en: Yeah, his name is Constable, but I keep calling him almost the constable also, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，他名字叫康斯特布尔，但我总是忍不住也叫他“警官”（Constable），是啊。

sentences.en: Decides to do is that, you know, he doesn't like all these people like using the park and maybe causing some maintenance issues with, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 他决定做的事是，你知道，他不喜欢这么多人利用公园，可能会造成一些维护问题，我不知道，

sentences.en: sitting down on blankets or something like that.
sentences.zh: 比如坐在毯子上之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And so he says that, well, you know, what you got to have to do is you need to reimburse the park department for maintenance,
sentences.zh: 所以他说，好吧，你知道，你必须要做的是你需要补偿公园管理局的维护费用，

sentences.en: and therefore that would require charging admission to Shakespeare in the park,
sentences.zh: 因此这就需要对“公园里的莎士比亚”收取门票，

sentences.en: which is against the sort of like deal that Papp had made with Robert Moses about doing Shakespeare in the park.
sentences.zh: 这违背了帕普与罗伯特·摩西关于在公园上演莎士比亚的协议。

sentences.en: And so it puts him in this bind.
sentences.zh: 这让他陷入了困境。

sentences.en: He has to, yeah, that he has promised, I will never charge for Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 他必须，是的，他承诺过，我绝不会对莎士比亚演出收费。

sentences.en: And he doesn't want to, but now he's being told you have to.
sentences.zh: 他不想收费，但现在有人告诉他必须收费。

sentences.en: And constable is sure that Moses would be like, yeah, get this subversive out of the park.
sentences.zh: 而康斯特布尔确信摩西会说，是的，把这个颠覆分子赶出公园。

sentences.en: I don't want him in there.
sentences.zh: 我不想让他待在那儿。

sentences.en: So he is one of those things where it's like my boss did the exact opposite, but I know he really wants me to do this because it aligns with the values I ascribe to him.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那种情况，我的老板做了完全相反的事，但我知道他真的想让我这么做，因为这符合我所认为的他的价值观。

sentences.en: And it's just, it's foolish.
sentences.zh: 这真是愚蠢。

sentences.en: Don't do that, people.
sentences.zh: 别那样做，伙计们。

sentences.en: Just do what the boss did, because that's what they want being done right now.
sentences.zh: 就照老板做的做，因为那才是他们现在想要完成的事情。

sentences.en: And you would think, again, that Moses would just overrule Mustache when he hears about, but like Roman, he was saying earlier,
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，摩西听到这件事后会直接否决那个留胡子的家伙，但就像罗曼之前说的，

sentences.en: one of these commandments that was ingrained in him in politics was you always have to support your subordinates.
sentences.zh: 他政治生涯中根深蒂固的准则之一就是你必须始终支持你的下属。

sentences.en: That's how you get their loyalty.
sentences.zh: 这就是你获得他们忠诚的方式。

sentences.en: You make them feel like you have their back all the time.
sentences.zh: 你得让他们觉得你永远是他们的后盾。

sentences.en: And in addition to that, if he says constable is wrong, then it's almost like saying he's wrong because he has invested constable with this power.
sentences.zh: 而且除此之外，如果他说康斯特布尔错了，那几乎就等于在说他自己错了，因为是他赋予了康斯特布尔这种权力。

sentences.en: So if his whole thing is infallibility, if the guy he hired is wrong, that means he's a little wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果他整个人设的基础是“绝不犯错”，那么他雇的人错了，就意味着他自己也错了一点点。

sentences.en: And so he had vowed publicly to his subordinates, I will never overrule you.
sentences.zh: 于是他公开向部下发誓：我绝不会推翻你们的决定。

sentences.en: And that's how I'm going to keep you loyal to me is I'm going to be loyal to you.
sentences.zh: 我就是这样让你们对我保持忠诚的，那就是我对你们保持忠诚。

sentences.en: So when Moses comes back, he backs up the mustache and refuses to talk to Pap.
sentences.zh: 所以当摩西回来时，他支持了“胡子男”，拒绝与帕普交谈。

sentences.en: And the money he said he'd raise for the Shakespeare Festival, that's not happening.
sentences.zh: 而他承诺为莎士比亚戏剧节筹集的资金，也没了下文。

sentences.en: And Moses writes Pap a letter saying, well, for maintenance, it's going to cost between $100,000 and $150,000 that you're going to have to reimburse the Parks Department.
sentences.zh: 摩西写信给帕普说，维护费用大概在10万到15万美元之间，这笔钱你得赔偿给公园管理处。

sentences.en: And, like, this is 1959.
sentences.zh: 要知道，这可是1959年。

sentences.en: Like, I mean, that's a lot of money now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这在现在都是一笔巨款。

sentences.en: That's an astronomical amount back then.
sentences.zh: 在当时那简直是个天文数字。

sentences.en: And Pap is trying to meet with Moses.
sentences.zh: 帕普试图和摩西会面。

sentences.en: But Moses is like, I'm not in charge.
sentences.zh: 但摩西却说，我不管这事。

sentences.en: Constable's in charge.
sentences.zh: 是康斯特布尔在管。

sentences.en: And I wonder if here it's a little bit loyalty and a little bit him trying to insulate himself from blame that, like, if there's constable between me and Pap,
sentences.zh: 我怀疑这其中既有一点忠诚的成分，也有他试图让自己免受指责的考量，就像是，如果我和帕普之间隔着一个康斯特布尔，

sentences.en: then Pap can't get mad at me.
sentences.zh: 那么帕普就没法对我发火了。

sentences.en: And constable keeps moving the goalposts.
sentences.zh: 而且康斯特布尔一直在变着法子刁难。

sentences.en: He's like, you've got to charge a $1 admission fee.
sentences.zh: 他说，你得收取1美元的入场费。

sentences.en: And Pap's like, OK, I'll consider it.
sentences.zh: 帕普说，好吧，我会考虑的。

sentences.en: Constable goes, OK, then it's $2 admission fee.
sentences.zh: 康斯特布尔又说，好吧，那入场费就是2美元。

sentences.en: And Pap starts to realize this is not about money.
sentences.zh: 帕普开始意识到，这根本不是钱的问题。

sentences.en: This is about the mustache thinks I'm a communiSt.
sentences.zh: 这是因为“胡子男”觉得我是个共产主义者。

sentences.en: And that's what it's about.
sentences.zh: 这才是问题的关键。

sentences.en: This is not a fair fight.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是一场公平的较量。

sentences.en: And I'm going to have to fight it like a fight.
sentences.zh: 我得像打仗一样去应对它。

sentences.en: And so what does he do?
sentences.zh: 那么他做了什么呢？

sentences.en: He uses the same tool the moms use.
sentences.zh: 他用了那些妈妈们用的同样手段。

sentences.en: He goes to the press.
sentences.zh: 他找了媒体。

sentences.en: What does he do, Roman?
sentences.zh: 他做了什么，罗曼？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No, he goes to the media and starts, like, you know, he starts to talk about Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 不，他是去找媒体，开始谈论莎士比亚。

sentences.en: These are all, like, educated people love Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 这些都是受过教育的人，他们热爱莎士比亚。

sentences.en: They are now at a point in Moses' career where the newspapers are criticizing Moses on a, you know, somewhat regular basis.
sentences.zh: 在摩西的职业生涯中，他们现在正处于一个报纸开始对他进行相对频繁批评的阶段。

sentences.en: And the funny thing here is he really goes for drama.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他真的开始大打戏剧牌了。

sentences.en: You know, like, he's going to kind of do the things that Robert Moses is known for.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他开始做那些罗伯特·摩西一贯擅长的事情。

sentences.en: It's like this sort of, like, attack on character, different sort of innuendo, you know, like, different things to sort of, like,
sentences.zh: 就像是一种人格攻击，各种影射，你知道，用各种手段来，

sentences.en: make it feel like there's a lot of corruption here, that Moses is a kind of villain here.
sentences.zh: 让人觉得这里面有很多腐败，摩西是个反派角色。

sentences.en: It doesn't, like, actually – I don't think it really highlights his role in the beginning of making it all possible, you know.
sentences.zh: 这并没有——我不认为这真正突出了他在最初促成这一切方面的作用，你知道。

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，完全没有。

sentences.en: He really – he makes it into a play, you know, and he's quoting Shakespeare all the time, and the reporters love that.
sentences.zh: 他真的把这变成了一场戏，他一直在引用莎士比亚，记者们很吃这一套。

sentences.en: And Moses responds in kind, and he tries to go back to his old playbook similarly, and he starts these, you know, innuendos behind the scenes about Pap being a red.
sentences.zh: 摩西也以牙还牙，试图用他那套老剧本回击，他在幕后散布关于帕普是“赤色分子”的影射。

sentences.en: But that used to work.
sentences.zh: 但这招以前管用。

sentences.en: Times have slightly changed.
sentences.zh: 时代已经变了。

sentences.en: This is not a time when it's okay to be a communist, but Joe McCarthy's been dead for a couple years.
sentences.zh: 现在不是共产主义者可以横行的时代了，而且乔·麦卡锡都已经死了好几年了。

sentences.en: There's – people kind of look back at that as gross.
sentences.zh: 人们回首往事时会觉得那很恶心。

sentences.en: They're not like, I love communism.
sentences.zh: 他们并不是说，我热爱共产主义。

sentences.en: Everyone should believe what they want, but they're like, that was gross.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有权相信自己想相信的，但他们会觉得，那做法太恶心了。

sentences.en: And they called – and so reporters, when they hear these rumors, they say this is McCarthyism in a disapproving way.
sentences.zh: 于是记者们听到这些谣言时，会以一种不赞同的口吻称之为“麦卡锡主义”。

sentences.en: And just as with the first Battle of Central Park, this story is getting simplified.
sentences.zh: 就像第一次中央公园之战一样，这个故事正在被简化。

sentences.en: Moses is the villain.
sentences.zh: 摩西是反派。

sentences.en: He hates free Shakespeare, something that is objectively good.
sentences.zh: 他讨厌免费的莎士比亚戏剧，而这客观上是一件好事。

sentences.en: You cannot argue that there is a downside to putting on free Shakespeare plays in the park.
sentences.zh: 你无法反驳在公园里上演免费莎士比亚戏剧有什么坏处。

sentences.en: You can't.
sentences.zh: 你反驳不了。

sentences.en: It's impossible.
sentences.zh: 这不可能。

sentences.en: And the thing is that they also do is they start to fact-check his claiMs.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还开始核实他的说法。

sentences.en: About what's going on in ways that they didn't used to do.
sentences.zh: 以一种过去从未有过的方式来核实正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: It used to be if Moses said something, that was the end of it.
sentences.zh: 过去如果摩西说了什么，那就是定论。

sentences.en: You didn't question it.
sentences.zh: 你不会去质疑它。

sentences.en: But now they're questioning it.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们开始质疑了。

sentences.en: And once again, public opinion turns against him.
sentences.zh: 舆论再次倒向了他对立面。

sentences.en: And Carol points out that in the past when there had been serious PR crises, Moses would get sick and be in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 卡罗尔指出，过去当出现严重的公关危机时，摩西就会装病住进医院。

sentences.en: And the same thing happens here for reasons that are never fully explained.
sentences.zh: 这次也发生了同样的事情，原因从未得到完全解释。

sentences.en: My pet theory is that he has a heart attack.
sentences.zh: 我个人的猜测是他心脏病发作了。

sentences.en: But who knows?
sentences.zh: 但谁知道呢？

sentences.en: You never know.
sentences.zh: 你永远不知道。

sentences.en: But he goes to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 但他确实去了医院。

sentences.en: And Carol says that photos of Moses leaving the hospital make him look for the first time old, like actually old, like an old weathered man.
sentences.zh: 卡罗尔说，摩西离开医院的照片让他看起来第一次显得苍老，就像一个饱经风霜的老人。

sentences.en: And then Pap is like, I'm going to put this – the onus of this on Mayor Wagner.
sentences.zh: 然后帕普说，我要把这个——把这个责任推给瓦格纳市长。

sentences.en: Mayor, overrule these policies.
sentences.zh: 市长，推翻这些政策吧。

sentences.en: And, of course, the mayor is like, I'd love to.
sentences.zh: 当然，市长会说，我很想这么做。

sentences.en: I'd love to just say, yeah, put Shakespeare in the park.
sentences.zh: 我很想直接说，好啊，在公园里上演莎士比亚戏剧吧。

sentences.en: But he can't overrule Moses.
sentences.zh: 但他无法推翻摩西的决定。

sentences.en: And it's almost like at this point the mayor must have felt so annoyed.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，市长一定感到非常恼火。

sentences.en: Moses is punishing the mayor just for considering it.
sentences.zh: 摩西仅仅因为市长考虑过这件事就在惩罚他。

sentences.en: He refuses to take Wagner's calls.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝接听瓦格纳的电话。

sentences.en: And Mayor Wagner becomes the subject of these joking headlines where Mayor Wagner will be like, I plan to talk to Moses later.
sentences.zh: 瓦格纳市长成了这些调侃头条的主角，比如瓦格纳市长会说，我计划稍后和摩西谈谈。

sentences.en: I can't quite get him.
sentences.zh: 我还没联系上他。

sentences.en: And so these headlines were like, Mayor searches for Moses.
sentences.zh: 所以这些头条新闻写着：市长寻找摩西。

sentences.en: Where is Moses?
sentences.zh: 摩西在哪里？

sentences.en: You know, Mayor can't find him.
sentences.zh: 你知道，市长找不到他。

sentences.en: And if I was Wagner, I'd be so pissed that I'm not even in a fight with Moses.
sentences.zh: 如果我是瓦格纳，我会气疯的，因为我甚至不是在和摩西打架。

sentences.en: I'm in a fight with the mustache.
sentences.zh: 我是在和那个“胡子男”打架。

sentences.en: And I'm looking like a fool because with a guy who shouldn't even – I shouldn't have to deal with, you know.
sentences.zh: 我看起来像个傻瓜，因为我竟然要和一个我根本不该打交道的人周旋。

sentences.en: And he can't fire Moses.
sentences.zh: 而且他还没法解雇摩西。

sentences.en: And so Wagner has to then support him and say, Moses is too valuable.
sentences.zh: 所以瓦格纳不得不支持他，说摩西太有价值了。

sentences.en: I can't do anything about it.
sentences.zh: 我对此无能为力。

sentences.en: And the press plays it as Wagner giving in to Moses.
sentences.zh: 媒体则将其解读为瓦格纳向摩西屈服。

sentences.en: So, again, if I'm Wagner, I'm like, I'm losing a fight with the mustache.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我是瓦格纳，我会想，我竟然输给了一个“胡子男”。

sentences.en: This is ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: And ultimately, Pap goes to the courts.
sentences.zh: 最终，帕普诉诸法律。

sentences.en: And a court finds narrowly, kind of for the first time, that Moses is being capricious with his power and that he cannot do that with the parks.
sentences.zh: 法院罕见地做出了裁决，这在某种程度上是第一次认定摩西滥用权力，他不能在公园问题上这样做。

sentences.en: And this is really stunning because, you know, this was the kind of thing that like in the previous court cases, the law was interpreted in such a way,
sentences.zh: 这真的很令人震惊，因为你知道，在之前的诉讼中，法律的解释方式，

sentences.en: written by Moses and interpreted in such a way that anything within the park walls, anything that related to parks whatsoever, was the complete domain of Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 是由摩西撰写并以某种方式解读的，即公园围墙内的任何事物，任何与公园有关的事物，都是罗伯特·摩西的绝对领地。

sentences.en: He was the king of the parks.
sentences.zh: 他是公园之王。

sentences.en: They could not – he could tear down any structure that he wanted, build any other one that he wanted.
sentences.zh: 他们无法——他可以拆除任何他想拆的建筑，建造任何他想建的建筑。

sentences.en: I mean like it was really – and for something related to like, you know, ephemeral exhibition of Shakespeare plays, to think that this is the thing that, you know, a non-permanent,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的很——对于像莎士比亚戏剧这种短暂的展览，认为这竟然是能阻止他的事情，这种非永久性的，

sentences.en: you know, cultural institution, just like – or even just like cultural like, I don't know, occurrence is the thing that stops him.
sentences.zh: 文化机构，或者仅仅是文化活动，竟然成了阻止他的东西。

sentences.en: And when it comes to court interpretation of what his power is inside of the parks is really stunning.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到法院对他在公园内权力的解释时，这真的很令人震惊。

sentences.en: This is a real change in his power.
sentences.zh: 这是他权力的一次真正转变。

sentences.en: It's huge.
sentences.zh: 这意义重大。

sentences.en: And again, if you're making a movie about Robert Moses, this is one of the things you do because the drama and the narrative is there because it's so simple.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，如果你要拍一部关于罗伯特·摩西的电影，这绝对是必拍情节，因为戏剧性和叙事感就在那里，因为它太简单了。

sentences.en: And it's like it's such an ephemeral thing.
sentences.zh: 而且这只是一件如此短暂的事情。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: But the story is so clear.
sentences.zh: 但这个故事非常清晰。

sentences.en: You know, it's such a clear story.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个非常清晰的故事。

sentences.en: And the only thing that screws up this story dramatically is Moses probably not really wanting to do it.
sentences.zh: 唯一破坏这个故事戏剧性的是摩西可能根本不想这么做。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the whole – just as we've been yelling this whole series, why don't you just accept its resignation?
sentences.zh: 就像我们这整个系列一直在喊的那样，为什么不直接接受他的辞职呢？

sentences.en: There's the part of me in here that's like just do it.
sentences.zh: 我内心深处有个声音在说，直接做吧。

sentences.en: Just swallow your loyalty philosophy and just do it because it's so obviously wrong, you know.
sentences.zh: 抛弃你那套忠诚哲学，直接做吧，因为这显然是错的，你知道。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But maybe this is like one of those things like if you eliminate the penny, people like begin to like understand that money has no meaning.
sentences.zh: 但也许这就像那种事情，如果你取消了便士，人们就会开始明白金钱毫无意义。

sentences.en: That money is not real.
sentences.zh: 金钱不是真实的。

sentences.en: And it's kind of one of those things like he knows that he's so propped up in this system of you just support your guys.
sentences.zh: 这就像那种情况，他知道自己在这个“支持自己人”的体系中得到了极大的支撑。

sentences.en: I – you know, the mayor just supports me.
sentences.zh: 我——你知道，市长支持我。

sentences.en: The governor just supports me.
sentences.zh: 州长支持我。

sentences.en: Like, you know, they trust me to do it.
sentences.zh: 他们信任我能把事情办成。

sentences.en: And so I think that this is really something that he can't possibly move on mostly because he knows that the whole structure that holds him in place is at the base level this thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这确实是他无法妥协的事情，主要是因为他知道支撑他地位的整个结构，在底层就是这种逻辑。

sentences.en: You know, of this idea of like I trust your judgment because you are you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是这种“我信任你的判断，因为你是你”的想法。

sentences.en: That's what he depends on for the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 这就是他依赖报纸的原因。

sentences.en: That's what he depends on for his relationship in politics as he, you know, remains this bureaucrat inside of, you know, this constantly changing political machinery.
sentences.zh: 这就是他依赖政治关系的原因，因为他始终是这个不断变化的政治机器中的官僚。

sentences.en: And so I get it.
sentences.zh: 所以我明白了。

sentences.en: I get that this is the thing that he can't change on.
sentences.zh: 我明白这就是他无法改变的地方。

sentences.en: It makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这说得通。

sentences.en: It's like when we talked to AOC, she was talking about how like so much of politics is based on if you give your word, can you keep it?
sentences.zh: 就像我们和AOC交谈时，她谈到政治很大程度上取决于如果你许下诺言，你能否信守？

sentences.en: Do you have the power and the strength to keep it if you promise something or if you say you're going to support something or go against something?
sentences.zh: 如果你承诺了什么，或者你说你要支持什么或反对什么，你是否有权力和力量去坚持？

sentences.en: And this is one of those times you're right.
sentences.zh: 这是其中一次，你说得对。

sentences.en: Yeah, he has to maintain that power of saying like, no, when I say something, it happens.
sentences.zh: 是的，他必须保持那种权力，即说出“不，我说什么就是什么”的威信。

sentences.en: But Carol points out that based on precedent, Moses could have appealed this court case and won.
sentences.zh: 但卡罗尔指出，根据先例，摩西本可以上诉并赢得这场官司。

sentences.en: Yeah, for sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: But instead he says, I'll abide by the decision.
sentences.zh: 但他却说，我会遵守裁决。

sentences.en: We'll have Shakespeare in the park.
sentences.zh: 我们会在公园里上演莎士比亚戏剧。

sentences.en: And he tries to arrange the money Pap needs to get the festival back into the park.
sentences.zh: 他还试图筹集帕普让戏剧节重返公园所需的资金。

sentences.en: And Pap only has time for one play.
sentences.zh: 而帕普只来得及排演一部戏。

sentences.en: He puts on Julius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 他上演了《朱利叶斯·凯撒》。

sentences.en: It's a huge triumph.
sentences.zh: 这是一次巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: Everybody loves it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都喜欢它。

sentences.en: I think it's very funny that he probably did it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很有趣的是，他可能真的这么做了。

sentences.en: Maybe he didn't purpose the story of a potential tyrant being taken down, you know.
sentences.zh: 也许他不是故意要讲一个潜在暴君被推翻的故事，你知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: And Carol wonders, he says, why did Moses give up this fight when previously he had never admitted defeat so relatively easily?
sentences.zh: 卡罗尔感到好奇，他说，为什么摩西在以前从未如此轻易承认失败的情况下，这次却放弃了这场斗争？

sentences.en: And he says, one explanation is that Moses could see the damage it was doing to his public image.
sentences.zh: 他说，一种解释是摩西看到了这对他的公众形象造成的损害。

sentences.en: But Carol ultimately, he's like, I think that Moses just didn't want to fight this battle in the first place and got dragged into it because of Constable's dumb choices.
sentences.zh: 但卡罗尔最终认为，摩西根本不想打这场仗，只是因为康斯特布尔的愚蠢选择而被拖下水了。

sentences.en: And he seems to have mired Pap so much that he let it happen.
sentences.zh: 他似乎把帕普逼得太紧，以至于他不得不让事情发生。

sentences.en: And he eventually builds the Delacorte amphitheater in the park expressly as a permanent home for Pap's productions.
sentences.zh: 他最终在公园里建造了德拉科特露天剧场，明确作为帕普作品的永久基地。

sentences.en: And so Sid Shapiro, he suspects and he says to Carol that he thinks Moses wanted to lose this one.
sentences.zh: 所以希德·夏皮罗怀疑并对卡罗尔说，他认为摩西想输掉这一场。

sentences.en: That like if ever there was a battle that Moses not just was okay with losing but didn't want to win, you know, on the merits, this is it.
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么战斗是摩西不仅愿意输，甚至不想赢的，那肯定就是这一场。

sentences.en: And Carol goes on to talk about Joe Papp.
sentences.zh: 卡罗尔接着谈到了乔·帕普。

sentences.en: This fight was one of the best things that ever happened to Joe Papp.
sentences.zh: 这场斗争是乔·帕普一生中遇到的最好的事情之一。

sentences.en: He's the darling of the liberal elites.
sentences.zh: 他成了自由派精英们的宠儿。

sentences.en: He becomes this institution in the theater world.
sentences.zh: 他在戏剧界成了这所机构的代名词。

sentences.en: He founds the public theater eventually down by Astor Place, which is still there.
sentences.zh: 他最终在阿斯特广场附近建立了公共剧院，至今仍在那里。

sentences.en: But for Moses, it's another blow to his reputation is another demonstration of just how much power he has over the mayor, which people are starting to realize.
sentences.zh: 但对摩西来说，这又是对他声誉的一次打击，也再次证明了他对市长拥有多大的权力，人们也开始意识到这一点。

sentences.en: And the press turns further against it.
sentences.zh: 媒体也进一步倒戈反对他。

sentences.en: They see that Constable is kind of this mini version of the boss, that this arrogance is just his boss's arrogance.
sentences.zh: 他们看出康斯特布尔就像是老板的迷你版，这种傲慢不过是他老板傲慢的体现。

sentences.en: And now it's not just the young go-getters who are looking to get Moses.
sentences.zh: 现在，不仅是那些想搞垮摩西的年轻进取者在盯着他。

sentences.en: It's the establishment as well.
sentences.zh: 连建制派也开始行动了。

sentences.en: And even the Times starts to investigate Moses' Title I projects.
sentences.zh: 甚至《泰晤士报》也开始调查摩西的“第一章”项目。

sentences.en: And the new frame for the media isn't Moses the hero who occasionally maybe I don't know if he's wrapped up in something.
sentences.zh: 媒体对他的描述不再是那个偶尔——我不知道他是否卷入了什么——的英雄摩西。

sentences.en: We'll see.
sentences.zh: 我们走着瞧。

sentences.en: But Moses, the villain.

sentences.zh: 所以我们将在下一章见到一个人。

sentences.en: He's a very fun person to talk about.
sentences.zh: 他是一个谈论起来非常有趣的人。

sentences.en: Who is going to be a little bit more than Moses can handle.
sentences.zh: 他将成为摩西难以应付的角色。

sentences.en: But this guy has an accomplice.
sentences.zh: 但这家伙有一个同谋。

sentences.en: And that accomplice's name is Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 而那个同谋的名字叫罗伯特·摩西。

sentences.en: Because as Caro says, only Robert Moses could lose Robert Moses his power.
sentences.zh: 因为正如卡罗所说，只有罗伯特·摩西才能让罗伯特·摩西失去权力。

sentences.en: And he did.
sentences.zh: 而他确实做到了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This is chapter 46.
sentences.zh: 这是第46章。

sentences.en: And it's just called Nelson.
sentences.zh: 标题就叫“纳尔逊”。

sentences.en: It's not about the band Nelson.
sentences.zh: 不是关于那个叫“纳尔逊”的乐队。

sentences.en: I'm sorry, everybody.
sentences.zh: 抱歉了，各位。

sentences.en: It stands for Nelson Rockefeller.
sentences.zh: 它指的是纳尔逊·洛克菲勒。

sentences.en: And oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: This is it.
sentences.zh: 就是他了。

sentences.en: This is it.
sentences.zh: 就是他了。

sentences.en: Buckle up.
sentences.zh: 系好安全带。

sentences.en: This is the chapter you've been waiting for.
sentences.zh: 这就是你们一直期待的章节。

sentences.en: You've sat through hours and hours of us talking,
sentences.zh: 你们听我们讲了几个小时，

sentences.en: waiting for Moses to finally get what he was getting.
sentences.zh: 等着看摩西最终得到他应得的下场。

sentences.en: And this is when he gets it.
sentences.zh: 而这就是他遭殃的时候。

sentences.en: It's Nelson.
sentences.zh: 是纳尔逊。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, the Nelson here, as she says, Nelson Rockefeller.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这里的纳尔逊，正如她所说，是纳尔逊·洛克菲勒。

sentences.en: In 1959, he is the new New York governor.
sentences.zh: 1959年，他是新任纽约州州长。

sentences.en: And Nelson Rockefeller, Caro tells us, he's a little different from the previous governors that Moses has dealt with.
sentences.zh: 卡罗告诉我们，纳尔逊·洛克菲勒与摩西之前打交道的州长们有点不同。

sentences.en: He is not quite the same type of politician.
sentences.zh: 他不是那种类型的政客。

sentences.en: What's the reason for this?
sentences.zh: 原因是什么呢？

sentences.en: Because Nelson Rockefeller, as you can tell from his last name, is enormously rich, like cosmically rich.
sentences.zh: 因为纳尔逊·洛克菲勒，正如你从他的姓氏就能看出的，非常有钱，简直是富可敌国。

sentences.en: Absolutely rich.
sentences.zh: 绝对的富有。

sentences.en: And they're basically, you know, he mentions that the Rockefeller family has basically been bankrolling the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 他提到洛克菲勒家族基本上一直在资助共和党。

sentences.en: Basically, like it pays for the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 基本上，就是由他们来买单。

sentences.en: So anything that they want to do, you know, it's just up to him and his family.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想做的任何事，你知道，都取决于他和他的家族。

sentences.en: So, like the idea that Moses controls a lot of money, it's just nonsense to him.
sentences.zh: 所以，摩西控制着大量资金这种想法，对他来说简直是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: No, this is a guy.
sentences.zh: 不，这就是那个人。

sentences.en: This is a guy like that.
sentences.zh: 就是那种人。

sentences.en: His grandfather was the richest man possibly in the world, you know, when he was alive.
sentences.zh: 他的祖父在世时可能是世界上最富有的人。

sentences.en: This is a guy who, Caro talks about, he has a ranch in Venezuela that is five times as large as the combined boroughs of New York City.
sentences.zh: 卡罗提到，他在委内瑞拉有一个牧场，面积是纽约市五个行政区总和的五倍。

sentences.en: Like, this guy owns so much.
sentences.zh: 这家伙拥有的东西太多了。

sentences.en: His brother controls Chase Manhattan Bank.
sentences.zh: 他的兄弟控制着大通曼哈顿银行。

sentences.en: At the time, Caro says, probably the most powerful financial institution in the world.
sentences.zh: 卡罗说，在当时，这可能是世界上最有权势的金融机构。

sentences.en: They have a controlling stake in Con Edison, where almost everyone gets their power from.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有联合爱迪生公司的控股权，几乎每个人都从那里获取电力。

sentences.en: Like, it's, they are so rich and they have so many sources of power in a way that Robert Moses just can't, with his rinky dink bridges, you know, his authorities, things like that,
sentences.zh: 他们太有钱了，拥有如此多的权力来源，而罗伯特·摩西那些破旧的桥梁、他的管理局之类的东西，

sentences.en: like just can't do it.
sentences.zh: 根本无法与之相比。

sentences.en: This family is so powerful that Nelson's brother, David Rockefeller, his lawyer is former governor Thomas Dewey.
sentences.zh: 这个家族太强大了，以至于纳尔逊的兄弟大卫·洛克菲勒的律师是前州长托马斯·杜威。

sentences.en: Like, one of the major governors is his, works for him.
sentences.zh: 像这样一位重量级州长竟然为他工作。

sentences.en: You know, it's crazy.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And so Nelson Rockefeller is like, I want to be governor.
sentences.zh: 所以纳尔逊·洛克菲勒说，我想当州长。

sentences.en: And he basically buys his way into office.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是花钱买通了通往职位的道路。

sentences.en: Also plays politics well.
sentences.zh: 而且他也很擅长政治博弈。

sentences.en: This is a guy, he's going to run for president years later.
sentences.zh: 他后来还会竞选总统。

sentences.en: He's going to be vice president years later.
sentences.zh: 多年后他还会成为副总统。

sentences.en: He's a real political figure.
sentences.zh: 他是一个真正的政治人物。

sentences.en: And he's good also, in a way that other governors have not been, at visualizing the pros and the cons of big building plans.
sentences.zh: 而且他与以往的州长不同，他很擅长从宏观上审视大型建筑计划的利弊。

sentences.en: He can't think of these big plans, but he's really good at looking at someone else's plan for a massive project and seeing what's good or what's bad about it.
sentences.zh: 他自己想不出这些宏大的计划，但他非常擅长审视别人的大型项目计划，并看出其中的优劣。

sentences.en: And he was really heavily involved in Rockefeller Center when it was a new thing, when he was 30 years old, when his father was building it.
sentences.zh: 当他30岁、他父亲建造洛克菲勒中心时，他就深度参与其中。

sentences.en: And so as governor, he has these big building plans that he wants to do.
sentences.zh: 所以作为州长，他也有自己想要实施的大型建筑计划。

sentences.en: And so he has that in common with Robert Moses, that he has big infrastructure dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 这一点他和罗伯特·摩西很像，都有宏大的基础设施梦想。

sentences.en: What he also has in common with Robert Moses is he is incredibly arrogant.
sentences.zh: 他和罗伯特·摩西的另一个共同点是，他极其傲慢。

sentences.en: He's incredibly stubborn.
sentences.zh: 他极其固执。

sentences.en: And Caro describes it as a serene sense that because his motives are pure, his decisions are right.
sentences.zh: 卡罗将其描述为一种宁静的信念：因为他的动机是纯粹的，所以他的决定就是正确的。

sentences.en: Like, he's wealthy.
sentences.zh: 他很有钱。

sentences.en: He's a wealthy man.
sentences.zh: 他是个富人。

sentences.en: He's always been wealthy.
sentences.zh: 他一直都很富有。

sentences.en: He was born basically with the assumption, what I want is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 他生来就有一种假设：我想要的就一定会发生。

sentences.en: And I want it, so it must be the right thing.
sentences.zh: 既然我想要，那它一定是正确的事情。

sentences.en: And Caro says Rockefeller's arrogance, it's different from the abrasive, hard arrogance of Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 卡罗说，洛克菲勒的傲慢与罗伯特·摩西那种尖锐、强硬的傲慢不同。

sentences.en: Robert Moses has this kind of like poking you arrogance, whereas Nelson Rockefeller's is the easy, gracious arrogance of someone who does not have to prove himself,
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·摩西有一种咄咄逼人的傲慢，而纳尔逊·洛克菲勒的傲慢是一个不需要证明自己的人所拥有的那种从容、优雅的傲慢，

sentences.en: who just takes it for granted.
sentences.zh: 一种理所当然的态度。

sentences.en: You will listen to me.
sentences.zh: 你会听我的。

sentences.en: And he is ruthless, but he's ruthless in a way that assumes I will win.
sentences.zh: 他很无情，但他的无情建立在“我一定会赢”的假设之上。

sentences.en: And it's something that Robert Moses has never really had to face ever in his career.
sentences.zh: 这是罗伯特·摩西职业生涯中从未真正面对过的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, what the two share is this love of cosplaying in a hard hat.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，两人共同点是都喜欢戴着安全帽装模作样。

sentences.en: They both love that thing.
sentences.zh: 他们都喜欢那一套。

sentences.en: Yes, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Neither of them are engineers or construction contractors, but they like to be around a site.
sentences.zh: 他们都不是工程师或建筑承包商，但他们喜欢出现在工地上。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And they understand the power of money.
sentences.zh: 而且他们都懂得金钱的力量。

sentences.en: And what's so funny is up until like the previous thousand pages, what Caro has, you know, really demonstrated is that these nickels and dimes, you know,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，直到前一千页，卡罗真正展示的是这些零碎的钱，你知道，

sentences.en: what fortune they amass to make Robert Moses able to do what he has done.
sentences.zh: 他们积累了多少财富才让罗伯特·摩西能够做到他所做的一切。

sentences.en: And then right at this moment when Nelson Rockefeller enters the scene, all of a sudden they're nickels and dimes again.
sentences.zh: 而就在纳尔逊·洛克菲勒登场的这一刻，突然间这些钱又变成了零钱。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: And it's like, you don't understand what money is.
sentences.zh: 就像是，你不懂什么才是钱。

sentences.en: And it's it's really something.
sentences.zh: 这真的很特别。

sentences.en: If there is ever a guy who is burning thousand dollar bills to light his cigars, like it's this guy.
sentences.zh: 如果说有人会烧掉千元大钞来点雪茄，那肯定就是这家伙。

sentences.en: So, yeah, all the change that commuters are throwing in is nothing.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，通勤者们扔进去的所有零钱根本不算什么。

sentences.en: And Caro says, survey the whole vast cast of characters on the New York political scene.
sentences.zh: 卡罗说，审视一下纽约政治舞台上庞大的角色阵容。

sentences.en: And there was only one man who could with impunity confront and defeat Robert Moses, the man who is now governor.
sentences.zh: 只有一个人能够毫无顾忌地对抗并击败罗伯特·摩西，那就是现在的州长。

sentences.en: Like this is this is going to be bad for Moses.
sentences.zh: 这对摩西来说可不是什么好事。

sentences.en: And Caro's like, Moses should see this.
sentences.zh: 卡罗认为，摩西应该看清这一点。

sentences.en: He should recognize how tough Rockefeller is going to be.
sentences.zh: 他应该意识到洛克菲勒会有多强硬。

sentences.en: But the old Moses is no longer interested in kind of understanding who he's up againSt.
sentences.zh: 但老摩西已经不再有兴趣去了解他的对手是谁了。

sentences.en: And Moses and Rockefeller have a history.
sentences.zh: 摩西和洛克菲勒是有渊源的。

sentences.en: He's worked with the Rockefeller family.
sentences.zh: 他曾与洛克菲勒家族共事。

sentences.en: He's worked with Nelson Rockefeller.
sentences.zh: 他曾与纳尔逊·洛克菲勒共事。

sentences.en: Like Nelson Rockefeller worked with him on getting the U.N.
sentences.zh: 比如纳尔逊·洛克菲勒曾与他合作争取联合国总部落地。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So like they've worked together.
sentences.zh: 所以他们曾一起工作过。

sentences.en: He thinks he has the measure of him.
sentences.zh: 他认为自己已经摸透了对方。

sentences.en: And Moses is in his 70s.
sentences.zh: 摩西已经70多岁了。

sentences.en: Rockefeller is 50.
sentences.zh: 洛克菲勒50岁。

sentences.en: And so Moses is like, this young man, I can be fatherly towards him.
sentences.zh: 所以摩西觉得，这个年轻人，我可以对他展现父辈般的关怀。

sentences.en: I can assume his support because I think he kind of sees him like Wagner, where Wagner is like, I'm a young man.
sentences.zh: 我可以理所当然地认为他会支持我，因为我觉得他看待洛克菲勒就像看待瓦格纳一样，瓦格纳会说：我是个年轻人，

sentences.en: Moses is an old man.
sentences.zh: 摩西是个老人。

sentences.en: I look up to him.
sentences.zh: 我尊敬他。

sentences.en: I have to listen to him.
sentences.zh: 我必须听他的。

sentences.en: And the difference, again, is that Wagner is not colossally like globally rich in the way that Rockefeller is.
sentences.zh: 但区别在于，瓦格纳并不像洛克菲勒那样拥有全球性的巨额财富。

sentences.en: And so conflict seems inevitable.
sentences.zh: 所以冲突似乎不可避免。

sentences.en: They're huge, arrogant fish in this New York State-sized pond.
sentences.zh: 他们是纽约州这个池塘里两条巨大而傲慢的鱼。

sentences.en: And there's one early point of conflict.
sentences.zh: 早期有一个冲突点。

sentences.en: Rockefeller has this aide who's a former NYU professor, go NYU, my own water, William J.
sentences.zh: 洛克菲勒有一位助手，是前纽约大学教授，威廉·J·罗南，

sentences.en: Ronan, who has sparred with Moses in the past and recommended abolishing the State Council of Parks and putting it under the Department of Conservation.
sentences.zh: 他过去曾与摩西发生过争执，并建议废除州公园委员会，将其置于自然资源保护部之下。

sentences.en: And Moses is like, nope, that's not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 摩西的态度是：不行，这不可能发生。

sentences.en: And nothing happens.
sentences.zh: 结果什么也没发生。

sentences.en: And I think Moses takes from that, oh, I can push these people around the same way that I pushed everyone else around.
sentences.zh: 我想摩西从中得出的结论是：哦，我可以像摆布其他人一样摆布这些人。

sentences.en: But Rockefeller starts intruding on the territory that Moses considers his territory, essentially parks and Long Island parks especially.
sentences.zh: 但洛克菲勒开始侵入摩西认为是自己领地的区域，主要是公园，特别是长岛的公园。

sentences.en: And Nelson Rockefeller's brother Lawrence, his name is spelled L-A-U, like the fancy way of spelling Lawrence, not L-A-W like the normal people would.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊·洛克菲勒的兄弟劳伦斯，他的名字拼写是L-A-U，那种花哨的拼法，而不是普通人用的L-A-W。

sentences.en: And he starts getting involved in having the state acquire more parkland.
sentences.zh: 他开始参与推动州政府收购更多的公园用地。

sentences.en: And Moses is like, great, I want more parkland.
sentences.zh: 摩西说：太好了，我想要更多的公园用地。

sentences.en: But in 1960, Rockefeller wants this massive state mass transit program put into place.
sentences.zh: 但在1960年，洛克菲勒想要实施一项大规模的州公共交通计划。

sentences.en: And transit is Moses' thing.
sentences.zh: 而交通正是摩西的地盘。

sentences.en: And he puts Ronan, Moses' new nemesis.
sentences.zh: 于是他启用了罗南，也就是摩西新的克星。

sentences.en: He makes him his closest advisor and has him looking at this program.
sentences.zh: 他让他成为自己最亲密的顾问，并让他负责审视这个项目。

sentences.en: And the first big battle that's kind of around these kind of shared interests that they're going to squabble over is over Moses' age.
sentences.zh: 而他们之间围绕这些共同利益产生的第一场大冲突，也是他们争执不下的焦点，就是摩西的年龄问题。

sentences.en: Like I said, he's 70 years old at this point.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，他当时已经70岁了。

sentences.en: When Rockefeller becomes governor, 65 is the mandated state retirement age.
sentences.zh: 当洛克菲勒就任州长时，州政府规定的强制退休年龄是65岁。

sentences.en: Legally, if you work for the state, you have to retire at 65 unless the governor signs an age extension and you can sign them for up to two years.
sentences.zh: 从法律上讲，如果你为州政府工作，必须在65岁退休，除非州长签署延期令，而且每次最多只能签两年。

sentences.en: And previous governors, they would sign them as early as possible.
sentences.zh: 以前的州长通常会尽早签署这些延期令。

sentences.en: They'd sign them for two years.
sentences.zh: 他们会直接签满两年。

sentences.en: Rockefeller will only give Moses one-year extensions, and he always waits as close to Moses' birthday as possible.
sentences.zh: 但洛克菲勒只给摩西一年一年的延期，而且总是拖到摩西生日临近时才签。

sentences.en: So in the days leading up to Moses' birthday, which should be a time for excited celebration,
sentences.zh: 所以，在摩西生日前夕，本该是一个令人兴奋的庆祝时刻，

sentences.en: instead he is agonizing over whether the governor is going to sign this extension and let him keep his jobs.
sentences.zh: 他却在为州长是否会签署这份延期令、让他保住职位而备受煎熬。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，没错。

sentences.en: Which really begins to eat at him.
sentences.zh: 这确实开始让他感到心力交瘁。

sentences.en: I mean, like, you can tell that, well, at least as Caro describes it, you know, he is an older man.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以看出，至少按照卡罗的描述，他确实是个老人了。

sentences.en: He's perceived as an older man.
sentences.zh: 他被视为一个老人。

sentences.en: He has these hearing aids.
sentences.zh: 他戴着助听器。

sentences.en: He can't hear as well.
sentences.zh: 他的听力大不如前。

sentences.en: You know, they think that maybe this is one of the reasons why Rockefeller, like, feels like he can do this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们认为这可能就是洛克菲勒觉得可以对他下手的原因之一。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Because the world is perceiving Moses as older, too.
sentences.zh: 因为外界也觉得摩西老了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I have to assume when you're in a meeting with Moses, he probably comes off as very old.
sentences.zh: 我不得不假设，当你和摩西开会时，他给人的感觉可能非常老迈。

sentences.en: Caro describes him as not really being able to hear what people are saying, so he just kind of assumes what people will say,
sentences.zh: 卡罗描述说，他其实已经听不清别人在说什么了，所以他只是凭猜测来回应别人，

sentences.en: which reminds me of a story about my wife's grandmother that she refused to wear a hearing aid.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起我妻子祖母的一个故事，她拒绝佩戴助听器。

sentences.en: At one point, she was eating dinner with their family, and her dad said something about, like, how's the food?
sentences.zh: 有一次，她和家人一起吃晚饭，她父亲问了句类似“饭菜怎么样”的话，

sentences.en: Coming up, our conversation with Brennan Lee Mulligan, host of the Dungeons & Dragons show, Dimension 20.

sentences.en: All because of one reason.
sentences.zh: 全是因为一个原因。

sentences.en: Our big bad, our villain of season one of The Unsleeping City was none other than undead Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 我们第一季《不眠之城》的大反派，不是别人，正是亡灵罗伯特·摩西。

sentences.en: Oh no, here he comes.

sentences.en: That's right.

sentences.en: Brennan created The Unsleeping City and made the main villain a fictionalized, magical Robert Moses.

sentences.en: You see Robert raises his hand, a seam opens in his wrist, and a rope of blood shoots out of his arm around the child.

sentences.en: When Brennan develops his stories for Dimension 20, he pushes the bounds of traditional D&D campaigns.

sentences.en: His first season was called Fantasy High, which Brennan describes as a John Hughes movie with swords and magic.

sentences.en: But there's something very different about looking to the power broker for source material.

sentences.en: But first, a quick primer on Dungeons & Dragons for those of you who may not be super familiar with the game.
